title: How Teams Structure .claude/ Across Org, Project & Developer Layers
label: 09.5 — The Claude Configuration Cascade
text: 09.5 — The Claude Configuration Cascade How Teams Structure .claude/ Across Org, Project & Developer Layers CLAUDE.md and .claude/ aren't just one file in one folder — they cascade. Org-wide rules, project-specific context, and personal preferences compose automatically as Claude walks up the directory tree. Here's how to architect the layers so team-shared rules stay in git, personal preferences stay local, and nothing gets duplicated. The .claude/ directory (project layer) .claude/ at project root · committed to git · shared with team The project-level .claude/ folder is the control center for Claude Code. It defines instructions, custom commands, permission rules, and specialized agent behaviors for everyone working in the repo. CLAUDE.md Central instruction manual. Claude reads it at session start for project context, architecture, and coding standards. settings.json Permission controls — which tools (bash, read, write) are allowed, which files or commands are denied, which MCP servers are available. rules/ Modular, markdown-based instructions. Rules without a paths field apply globally; others only when working in designated directories. commands/ Custom slash commands (e.g. /project:review ). Each markdown file becomes a command, with shell support via the ! prefix. skills/ Reusable, context-aware workflows. More advanced than commands — auto-invoked by Claude when relevant, not just triggered manually. agents/ Specialized subagents with defined personas and restricted tool access. Run risky tasks (reviews, audits) in isolated sessions. The ~/.claude/ directory (user layer) ~/.claude/ · personal to each developer · never committed to git The global folder holds personal preferences that apply across every project on your machine. It's yours alone — never mandate its contents across a team. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Global coding preferences — "always use TypeScript", "prefer functional style", personal workflow quirks. ~/.claude/projects/ Auto-memory store. Claude persists MEMORY.md per project so knowledge survives across sessions. commands/ & skills/ Personal commands and skills available everywhere, not scoped to one project. Your personal toolbox. Org and project .claude/ live in git. Only ~/.claude/ stays local. The config-cascade rule Cascading rules & precedence CLAUDE.md files are loaded by walking up the directory tree from the current working directory. Multiple CLAUDE.md files combine — each layer adds context without requiring duplication. When rules conflict, precedence flows: System policy ─▶ User (~/.claude/) ─▶ Project (.claude/) ← wins (floor) (personal prefs) (team-shared, highest) Project-level configuration takes highest precedence, ensuring team-shared rules always apply. System policy sets the safety floor. User preferences sit in between. Path-Scoped Rules Rules inside .claude/rules/ can declare a paths: field to apply only when Claude works in specific subdirectories (e.g. src/api/ ). Rules without paths apply project-wide. Use this to keep CLAUDE.md lean instead of overloading it with conditionals. Single-project layout .claude/ ├── settings.json # Permissions (allow bash, read files) ├── CLAUDE.md # High-level rules & project context ├── rules/ │ ├── api.md # Rules scoped to src/api/ │ └── tests.md # Testing conventions ├── commands/ │ └── review.md # /project:review slash command ├── skills/ │ └── secure-commit/ │ └── SKILL.md # Auto-invoked commit workflow └── agents/ └── code-reviewer.md # Isolated review subagent Multi-project org cascade Three layers — org (shared defaults), product (domain context), developer (personal). Org and product layers live in git; the developer layer stays local. my-org/ # Monorepo or org config repo ├── .claude/ # ━━ ORG LAYER ━━ shared defaults │ ├── CLAUDE.md # Org-wide tone, security, standards │ ├── settings.json # Default model, shared MCP servers │ ├── rules/ │ │ └── security.md # Non-negotiable security rules │ ├── commands/ │ │ └── review.md # Org-standard code review │ ├── skills/ │ │ └── code-style/SKILL.md # Org coding conventions │ └── agents/ │ └── sec-audit.md # Security audit subagent │ ├── product-a/ # ━━ PRODUCT LAYER ━━ domain context │ ├── .claude/ │ │ ├── CLAUDE.md # Architecture, stack, glossary │ │ ├── rules/ │ │ │ ├── api.md # REST patterns (paths: src/api/) │ │ │ └── migrations.md # DB migration rules │ │ ├── commands/ │ │ │ └── deploy.md # Product-specific deploy │ │ ├── skills/ │ │ │ └── workflow/SKILL.md │ │ └── agents/ │ │ └── reviewer.md # Domain-aware reviewer │ └── src/ │ ├── product-b/ # Different product, own .claude/ │ └── .claude/ │ ├── CLAUDE.md │ └── ... │ # ━━ DEVELOPER LAYER ━━ personal (not in git) ~/.claude/ ├── CLAUDE.md # "Always use TypeScript" ├── projects/ │ ├── product-a/MEMORY.md # Auto-persisted session memory │ └── product-b/MEMORY.md ├── commands/ │ └── standup.md # Personal shortcut └── skills/ └── my-workflow/SKILL.md 8 Recommendations for Teams 1. CLAUDE.md is your contract Org-level sets non-negotiable rules. Project-level extends with domain context. The directory tree walk combines them automatically — never duplicate. 2. Use rules/ for path scoping Don't overload CLAUDE.md with conditional logic. Put API rules in rules/api.md scoped to src/api/ , test rules in rules/tests.md . Modular and clean. 3. Skills are portable packages Encode repeatable workflows as SKILL.md directories. Any methodology becomes a mountable package any project can adopt. Skills auto-invoke — commands don't. 4. Agents isolate risky tasks Define subagents for sensitive operations — code reviews, security audits, dependency checks. They run in isolated sessions with restricted tool access. 5. Commands are the team API Slash commands ( /project:review , /project:deploy ) make workflows discoverable. Org commands set the floor; projects add domain-specific ones. 6. Let MEMORY.md accumulate Claude auto-persists session knowledge to ~/.claude/projects/*/MEMORY.md . Let it build context over time and review periodically for accuracy. 7. Version-control shared layers Org and project .claude/ live in git. Only ~/.claude/ stays local. Skills and agents are versioned and distributed like code. 8. Scope MCP servers per layer Org settings.json defines shared servers (Slack, Drive). Projects add domain-specific ones. Users add personal tools. Servers compose additively. Notable settings.json Keys Beyond permissions and MCP server lists, settings.json accepts several useful configuration keys: prUrlTemplate — Point the footer PR badge to a custom review URL instead of github.com. Still the answer for Bitbucket or GitHub Enterprise teams. As of v2.1.234, GitLab no longer needs the template for this: repos with a GitLab remote and an authenticated glab CLI get a native badge in the footer and statusline showing MR !N , with draft, pending, and green states. otelHeadersHelper — Path to a script that auto-refreshes OTEL auth tokens (runs every 29 min). As of v2.1.193, the equivalent MCP headersHelper also re-runs and reconnects automatically when a tool call returns 401 or 403 — token expiry no longer requires a session restart. See Monitoring section. disableAllHooks — Set true to disable all hooks globally (useful for troubleshooting). allowManagedHooksOnly — When set to true , only hooks distributed via managed settings (MDM/org policy) are allowed to run; user-defined hooks in project and user settings.json are blocked. Useful for enterprise environments that want to control hook execution centrally. requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion — Set via org managed settings to enforce a version range. Claude Code refuses to start if the installed version falls outside the range and directs the user to an approved version. Useful for enterprise compliance and rollout control. skillOverrides — Control per-skill model visibility: {"skill-name": "off"} hides from both model and / menu; "user-invocable-only" hides from model only; "name-only" sends name without description to the model. fallbackModel — Configure up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable. Works in both interactive and print ( -p ) mode. Pairs with the --fallback-model CLI flag for session-level overrides. As of v2.1.247, sub-agents that fail on their first model call with a 404 also fall back through this same chain instead of dying outright, and the error surfaced to the parent session includes the error type, status, request id, and model. settings.autoMode.hard_deny — Auto mode classifier rules that block unconditionally regardless of user intent or allow exceptions. Unlike regular deny rules (which the classifier can override when intent is clear), hard-deny rules are absolute. Use the same pattern array format as allow / deny rules in auto mode settings. Auto mode built-in safety blocks — Auto mode blocks certain destructive commands by default, independent of your deny rules: git reset --hard , git checkout -- . , git clean -fd , and git stash drop are blocked unless you explicitly asked to discard local work; git commit --amend is blocked when the commit wasn't made by the agent this session; terraform destroy , pulumi destroy , and cdk destroy are blocked unless you named the specific stack. Use settings.autoMode.hard_deny for additional custom blocks (v2.1.183). autoMode.classifyAllShell — When set to true , routes all Bash/PowerShell commands through the auto-mode classifier, not just arbitrary-code-execution patterns. Use to tighten auto-mode coverage so every shell command is evaluated — at the cost of slightly more classification overhead (v2.1.193). Auto mode reviews Monitor commands like Bash — Monitor tool allow rules are now set aside while auto mode is active, so Monitor commands go through the same auto-mode classifier review as Bash commands, instead of being auto-approved by a pre-existing allow rule (v2.1.236). autoMode settings location — autoMode configuration (including classifyAllShell , hard_deny , and disableAutoMode ) is not read from .claude/settings.local.json (the repo-resident, gitignored project-local file). Configure autoMode in ~/.claude/settings.json (user level) or the checked-in .claude/settings.json (project level) (v2.1.207). autoMode classifier model for external sessions — In auto mode, the permission classifier that evaluates whether tool calls require approval defaults to Sonnet 5 for external sessions (SDK, webhooks, headless claude -p runs). The model is validated on the session's first request and pinned for the rest of that session — ensuring consistent, low-latency classification for unattended pipelines without incurring per-call model-selection overhead (v2.1.210). Deny rule glob patterns — The tool-name position in deny rules now accepts glob patterns: "*" denies all tools. Allow rules reject non-MCP globs (only MCP tool name patterns are valid in allow rules). Unknown tool names in deny rules log a startup warning instead of being silently ignored. Tool(param:value) permission rule syntax — Match a tool's input parameters in permission rules using Tool(param:value) syntax. Supports * as a wildcard value. Example: Agent(model:opus) blocks subagents from spawning with the Opus model. Works in allow, deny, and ask positions (v2.1.178). disableBundledSkills — Set true to hide all bundled skills, workflows, and built-in slash commands from the model. Env var equivalent: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1 . Pairs with skillOverrides for per-skill granularity (v2.1.169). wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled — Set false to disable mouse-wheel scroll acceleration in fullscreen mode. Default is true . Useful if the default acceleration feels too fast when scrolling long outputs (v2.1.174). enforceAvailableModels — Enterprise managed setting. When enabled, the availableModels allowlist also constrains the Default model — a Default that would resolve to a disallowed model falls back to the first allowed model. User or project settings can no longer widen a managed availableModels list. Set via org/MDM managed settings only (v2.1.175). language — Pin the language Claude Code uses when auto-generating session titles. Without this setting, titles are generated in the language of the conversation. Accepts BCP 47 language tags (e.g. en , ja , fr ). Configurable at user or project level (v2.1.176). footerLinksRegexes — Array of regex patterns for footer-row link badges. Strings in the session footer matching a pattern are rendered as clickable link badges. Configurable at user or managed (MDM/org) settings level (v2.1.176). awsCredentialExport — Amazon Bedrock only. Path to a script or command that vends short-lived AWS credentials (e.g. via STS AssumeRole ). Credentials returned by the script are now cached until their Expiration field rather than a fixed 1-hour TTL — reducing unnecessary re-auth cycles for tokens with longer lifetimes (v2.1.176). attribution.sessionUrl — Set to false to omit the claude.ai session link from commits and PRs created in web and Remote Control sessions. Useful for teams that want clean commit attribution without embedding session URLs (v2.1.183). respondToBashCommands — Controls whether Claude automatically responds to the output of ! (bang) bash commands. Default is true as of v2.1.186: Claude reads the output and replies in-turn. Set to false to restore the previous context-only behavior where ! injects shell output without triggering a reply (v2.1.186). disableAutoMode — Set to true to opt out of auto mode on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Foundry. Auto mode is now enabled by default on these platforms as of v2.1.207 (no longer requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 ). Configure in user-level ~/.claude/settings.json or managed settings to keep manual permission prompts on cloud deployments (v2.1.207). axScreenReader — Set to true to enable screen reader mode — plain-text rendering optimized for screen readers. Equivalent to the --ax-screen-reader CLI flag or CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 env var (v2.1.208). vimInsertModeRemaps — Map two-key insert-mode sequences to special keys in vim mode. Example: {"vimInsertModeRemaps": {"jj": "Escape"}} lets you exit insert mode by typing jj quickly — a common vim muscle-memory shortcut (v2.1.208). Permission rule startup warnings for Write / NotebookEdit / Glob — As of v2.1.210, Claude Code logs a startup warning when your permission rules contain Write(path) , NotebookEdit(path) , or Glob(path) entries. Use Edit(path) to match file-write operations and Read(path) to match file-read/glob operations in your allow/deny rules — these more specific names target the correct tools without matching unintended operations (v2.1.210). workflowSizeGuideline — Set the advisory token-budget guideline for Dynamic workflow sessions (the "size guideline" shown to Claude when orchestrating large multi-agent runs). Configurable from any settings file (user, project, or managed). When set, the /config row for this setting is hidden from the config UI (v2.1.219). crossSessionInbound — Controls whether cross-session messages sent to a session running with bypassed permissions are held for your approval before delivery. Pairs with the v2.1.224 cross-session SendMessage / ListAgents capability (see Power Usage → Agent Teams). dialogExpiry — Sets how long a held cross-session message approval dialog stays pending before expiring. Messages to sessions without bypassed permissions auto-deliver regardless (v2.1.224). spellcheck — Optional. Set to true to underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type. Requires an aspell , hunspell , or ispell binary installed on the machine (v2.1.235). keybindingFlavor — Set to "readline" to make Ctrl+W in the prompt delete back to the previous whitespace, as in Bash; the default ( "classic" ) leaves Ctrl+W unchanged (v2.1.238). modelPicker — Curate the /model picker with an ordered, labeled list of models (any id spelling, including Vertex/Bedrock ids) — append to or replace the built-in lineup (v2.1.243). modelPricing — Managed setting: use an organization's contracted per-model rates and discount multiplier for /cost , the status line, and telemetry cost figures instead of list price. Configure via org/MDM managed settings (v2.1.243). Bash allow-rule wildcard-before-subcommand warning — As of v2.1.246, Claude Code logs a startup warning for Bash permission rules with a wildcard positioned before the subcommand (e.g. Bash(git * main) ), because such rules also match options inserted before the subcommand — unintentionally widening what the rule allows. Place wildcards after the subcommand (e.g. Bash(git commit *) ) to scope the rule precisely. feedbackDrafts — Set false to stop Claude from drafting a feedback report when something goes wrong in a session. When enabled (default), review and send the draft from /feedback (v2.1.247). spinnerTipsOverride — Customize the tips shown while Claude works. As of v2.1.247, accepts an array of {id, text, cooldownSessions, priority} entries (rotate your own tips alongside the built-in ones, with cooldown and priority control), a tipsFile path to load tips from an external file, and a label to distinguish org-supplied tips in the UI. Permission Allowlists & settings.local.json When you select "Always allow" at a Bash tool permission prompt, Claude Code writes that entry to .claude/settings.local.json — the gitignored, project-local layer. This means your personal approvals accumulate per-project without affecting teammates. To bulk-migrate common read-only patterns (grep, git diff, ls) into the allowlist at once, run /less-permission-prompts . Patterns & Anti-Patterns ✕ Copying CLAUDE.md into every repo Write once at the org level and inherit via the directory tree walk. Duplication guarantees drift. ✕ Domain rules at the org level Keep domain context at the project level. Org level is for cross-cutting standards only. ✕ One 2000-line CLAUDE.md Factor into rules/ with path scoping for modularity. Bloated CLAUDE.md files lose important rules in the noise. ✕ Mandating personal ~/.claude/ Let developers own their personal layer entirely. Enforcement belongs in the project .claude/ , not the user's home. ✕ Running sensitive tasks in the main session Define isolated agents/ with restricted permissions for audits, deploys, and anything touching credentials. ✕ Ignoring MEMORY.md Stale auto-memory poisons future sessions. Periodically review for accuracy and prune drift. External Memory: Obsidian & Markdown Vaults Claude's MEMORY.md is passive — session knowledge auto-persists as the model works. A curated markdown vault (Obsidian, Logseq, plain notes/ ) is the complement: intentional , human-authored, and portable across tools, models, and years. Andrej Karpathy popularized this pattern — a long-lived Obsidian vault of notes, decisions, and research that gets selectively fed into LLM sessions as high-signal context. The vault outlives any single model or IDE; the AI is just one of many readers. Practical integration patterns: Symlink a vault subfolder into the repo (e.g. docs/notes/ → ~/Obsidian/project-x/ ) so Claude reads it as part of the project tree. Paste relevant notes into context at session start — curated beats comprehensive. Wire an Obsidian / Reflect / Notion MCP server so Claude can search and append notes directly, turning the vault into a read/write memory layer. Treat the vault as source-of-truth; let MEMORY.md churn freely underneath it. Codex Equivalent OpenAI's Codex CLI uses the same layered architecture with different filenames: AGENTS.md instead of CLAUDE.md , .rules/ for guardrails, and .agents/skills/ for reusable workflows. The cascade model (org → project → user) is identical. See the Codex Best Practices page for the full mapping.

title: Connect Claude to Your Tools via MCP
label: 10 — Integrations
text: 10 — Integrations Connect Claude to Your Tools via MCP Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the universal adapter between AI models and your existing tools — databases, APIs, design tools, project management. 3rd-Party Model Providers Running Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI ? Use the interactive setup wizard: run claude , select "3rd-party platform" from the login screen, and follow the guided setup for authentication, region, and model pinning — no manual env var configuration needed. For Bedrock, if AWS_REGION is not set, Claude Code now reads the region from ~/.aws/config (matching AWS SDK precedence) — run /status to see which source is active (v2.1.172). Claude Code ──▶ MCP Protocol ──▶ JIRA ──▶ Figma ──▶ Notion ──▶ Azure DevOps ──▶ Google Workspace Setting Up MCP Connections via /plugin The fastest way to connect Claude Code to external tools is through the /plugin command. Plugins bundle MCP servers with OAuth — no API tokens or manual config needed. 1 Open the Plugin Browser In any Claude Code session, type /plugin and press Enter. This opens the interactive plugin browser showing all available plugins. 2 Select a Plugin to Install Browse the list and select the plugin you want (e.g., Atlassian, Figma, Notion). Press Enter to install it. Claude downloads the plugin and registers its MCP server automatically. 3 Authenticate via OAuth On first use of a plugin tool, Claude opens your browser for OAuth login (e.g., sign in with your Atlassian, Figma, or Notion account). This is a one-time step — credentials are cached for future sessions. 4 Verify the Connection Run /mcp to confirm the plugin's MCP server is connected and its tools are available. You should see the server listed with a green status. # Verify MCP connections /mcp # Example output: ✓ plugin:atlassian:atlassian — connected ✓ plugin:Notion:notion — connected ✓ plugin:figma:figma — connected Plugin vs. Manual MCP Config Use plugins for Jira, Figma, and Notion — they handle OAuth and updates automatically. Use manual mcpServers config in .claude/settings.json for tools without plugins (Azure DevOps, Google Workspace, custom servers). You can mix both approaches. Available Integrations JIRA MCP ▼ What it does: Read, create, and update JIRA issues directly from Claude. Search issues, transition statuses, add comments, and manage sprints without leaving the terminal. The easiest way to connect is via the Atlassian plugin , which uses Atlassian's hosted MCP endpoint with OAuth — no API tokens needed: // Plugin .mcp.json (managed automatically) { "mcpServers" : { "atlassian" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp" } } } Setup: Enable the atlassian plugin in Claude Code settings. Auth is handled via OAuth on first use — run /mcp to verify the connection. Example usage: "Create a JIRA ticket for this bug in the AUTH project" or "Show me all in-progress tickets assigned to me" Figma MCP ▼ What it does: Read Figma designs, extract component specs, colors, typography, and layout details. Implement designs with 1:1 visual fidelity directly from Figma files. Enable the Figma plugin in Claude Code settings. It uses Figma's hosted MCP endpoint with OAuth: // Plugin .mcp.json (managed automatically) { "mcpServers" : { "figma" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp" } } } Setup: Enable the figma plugin in Claude Code settings. Auth is handled via OAuth on first use — run /mcp to verify the connection. Example usage: "Implement the login page from this Figma file: [URL]" or "Extract the color palette from our design system" Notion MCP ▼ What it does: Search, read, create, and update Notion pages and databases. Pull specs from Notion, sync task status, and create documentation. Enable the Notion plugin in Claude Code settings. It uses Notion's hosted MCP endpoint with OAuth — no API tokens needed: // Plugin .mcp.json (managed automatically) { "mcpServers" : { "notion" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp" } } } Setup: Enable the Notion plugin in Claude Code settings. Auth is handled via OAuth on first use — run /mcp to verify the connection. Example usage: "Find the spec in Notion and implement the user stories" or "Create a Notion page documenting this API" Azure DevOps MCP ▼ What it does: Manage work items, repos, pipelines, wikis, test plans, and advanced security in Azure DevOps. Microsoft's official MCP server with browser-based OAuth — no PAT needed. // .claude/settings.json { "mcpServers" : { "ado" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "-y" , "@azure-devops/mcp" , "your-org-name" ] } } } Setup: Requires Node.js 20+. On first tool use, a browser window opens for Microsoft OAuth login — no PAT or env vars needed. Replace your-org-name with your Azure DevOps organization. See microsoft/azure-devops-mcp for details. Example usage: "List my ADO projects" or "List ADO builds for 'Contoso'" or "Create a work item in the Sprint 12 backlog" Google Workspace MCP ▼ What it does: Google offers hosted MCP servers for Google Cloud infrastructure (BigQuery, Cloud SQL, GKE, Compute Engine, etc.). Google Workspace products (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Gmail, Calendar) are not yet available as hosted MCP endpoints — use a community server for those. Google Cloud MCP (official, hosted) // .claude/settings.json — example: BigQuery { "mcpServers" : { "bigquery" : { "httpUrl" : "https://bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp" , "authProviderType" : "google_credentials" , "headers" : { "x-goog-user-project" : "your-project-id" } } } } Setup: Install gcloud CLI, run gcloud auth application-default login , then enable the MCP server: gcloud beta services mcp enable SERVICE --project=PROJECT_ID . See Google Cloud MCP docs for full instructions. Google Workspace MCP (community, self-hosted) # For Docs, Sheets, Drive, Gmail, Calendar # github.com/taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp git clone https://github.com/taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp cd google_workspace_mcp && cargo build --release claude mcp add google-workspace -- ./target/release/google_workspace_mcp Requires a Google Cloud project with OAuth credentials and the relevant APIs enabled. See the project README for setup. Example usage: "Read the PRD from this Google Doc and create a spec.md" or "Query the BigQuery dataset for last month's revenue" Tip You can run multiple MCPs simultaneously. title: Multi-Agent Code Review for Pull Requests
label: 10.5 — Code Review Agent
text: 10.5 — Code Review Agent Multi-Agent Code Review for Pull Requests A fleet of specialized agents examines your diff in parallel — catching logic errors, security vulnerabilities, edge cases, and regressions — then posts verified findings as inline PR comments. Prefer the Packaged Skill For local, pre-PR multi-agent review (7 specialists, consensus fan-out, severity-gated validation), use the code-review-team skill instead of or alongside GitHub's built-in Code Review Agent below. How the Multi-Agent Architecture Works ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Stage 1: Parallel Bug Detection │ │ │ │ Agent A: Logic errors ─┐ │ │ Agent B: Security vulns │ │ │ Agent C: Edge cases ├─► Candidate │ │ Agent D: Regressions │ Findings │ │ Agent E: Type safety ─┘ │ │ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Stage 2: Verification │ │ │ │ Each candidate checked against actual code │ │ behavior to filter out false positives │ │ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Stage 3: Ranking & Deduplication │ │ │ │ Results consolidated, ranked by severity, │ │ posted as inline PR comments │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Coverage on large PRs 84% of PRs over 1,000 lines receive at least one actionable finding, averaging 7.5 issues per review. Source: Anthropic internal telemetry, Claude Code review agent False positive rate <1% Verified agents filter noise before anything reaches the PR — comments you see are comments worth reading. Source: Anthropic internal telemetry, Claude Code review agent Setup Guide 1 Enable in Claude Admin Go to claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code , find the Code Review section, and click Setup . Requires a Claude Team or Enterprise subscription. 2 Install the Claude GitHub App Grant Contents , Issues , and Pull Requests read/write permissions. Select which repositories to enable — start with 1–2 repos to test. 3 Choose Your Review Trigger After PR creation only — runs once when opened (recommended to start). After every push — runs on each push, auto-resolves threads when issues are fixed. 4 Create a REVIEW.md Place a REVIEW.md at your repo root with review-specific rules. This file is read exclusively during code reviews, unlike CLAUDE.md which applies to all Claude interactions. Example REVIEW.md # Code Review Guidelines ## Always check - New API endpoints have corresponding integration tests - Database migrations are backward-compatible - Error messages don't leak internal details to users - No hardcoded secrets or credentials ## Style preferences - Prefer early returns over nested conditionals - Use structured logging, not f-string interpolation ## Skip - Generated files under src/gen/ - Formatting-only changes in *.lock files - Auto-generated migration files Reading the Results Each finding is posted as an inline comment tagged with a severity marker: Marker Meaning Action Red circle Bug — fix before merge Address immediately Yellow circle Nit — minor issue or style suggestion Address at your discretion Purple circle Pre-existing — bug not introduced by this PR Track for future cleanup Important Claude Code Review does not approve or block PRs. Your existing review workflows stay intact. Each comment includes a collapsible extended reasoning section explaining the agent's analysis. Alternative: GitHub Actions (Self-Hosted) If you prefer self-hosted review or are on a Pro plan, use claude-code-action on GitHub Marketplace: # .github/workflows/claude-review.yml name : Claude Code Review on : pull_request : types : [opened, synchronize, reopened] jobs : review : runs-on : ubuntu-latest steps : - uses : actions/checkout@v4 - uses : anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 with : anthropic_api_key : ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} review_mode : true Alternative: Local Review with Custom Subagents Create a custom code review subagent that runs locally before pushing: # .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md --- name : code-reviewer description : Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, and security issues tools : - Read - Grep - Glob - Bash --- Review the current git diff for: - Logic errors and potential bugs - Security vulnerabilities (injection, auth bypass, data exposure) - Missing error handling at system boundaries - Regressions against existing tests Only report findings you are confident about. Use a structured format: file, line, severity, description. Then run: Use the code-reviewer agent to review my staged changes When to Use It Best for Large PRs, AI-assisted code changes, cross-cutting refactors, PRs from newer team members, codebases with complex architectural invariants. Less useful for Tiny formatting-only diffs, instant gating needs (reviews take ~20 min), or as a full replacement for human review — it's designed to complement , not replace. Pro Tips Write specific rules in REVIEW.md for targeted findings. Start with one repo and evaluate quality. Use Claude for the first pass, humans for architectural and design decisions. Monitor spend at claude.ai/analytics/code-review — reviews average $15–25 each.

title: Turn Repeatable Workflows into Reusable Expert Modes
label: 11 — Building Your Own Skills
text: 11 — Building Your Own Skills Turn Repeatable Workflows into Reusable Expert Modes Skills are markdown directories that define specialized workflows. Claude loads them on demand — via slash commands or automatically by matching your task — providing consistency across sessions and team members. What are Skills? Skills are directories in .claude/skills/ containing a SKILL.md file plus optional supporting files (templates, scripts, reference docs). They turn tribal knowledge — code review checklists, deployment procedures, estimation frameworks — into repeatable, shareable workflows. Claude can auto-load skills by matching your task to skill descriptions, or you invoke them manually with /skill-name . Plugin skills use a namespace: /plugin:skill-name . Skill File Anatomy my-skill/ ├── SKILL.md # Required — skill content ├── reference.md # Optional — detailed docs ├── examples.md # Optional — usage examples └── scripts/ └── helper.py # Optional — executable scripts --- name : my-skill description : Reviews code for security issues. Use when auditing code. argument-hint : [file-or-directory] allowed-tools : Read Grep Bash(git *) disable-model-invocation : false --- # My Skill Review $ARGUMENTS for security issues. Skill directory: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} ## Process 1. First, do this 2. Then, check that 3. Finally, verify this Frontmatter Reference (All Fields) ▼ Field Type Description name string Display name and /slash-command . Defaults to directory name. description string What the skill does. Claude uses this for auto-invocation matching. Front-load the key use case. Truncated at 1,536 chars (startup warning shown when exceeded). argument-hint string Hint shown in autocomplete (e.g. [filename] , [issue-number] ). disable-model-invocation boolean If true , only you can invoke via /name — Claude won't auto-load. Use for side effects (deploy, send). user-invocable boolean If false , hidden from / menu. Claude can still auto-load. Use for background knowledge. allowed-tools string/list Tools Claude can use without prompting (e.g. Read Bash(grep:*) Bash(git *) ). On native macOS/Linux builds, Grep and Glob are embedded in the Bash tool — use Bash(grep:*) and Bash(find:*) instead. disallowed-tools string/list Tools to remove from the model while this skill is active (e.g. WebSearch Bash ). Inverse of allowed-tools — use to restrict capabilities for focused or safety-critical skills. model string Override model when skill is active (e.g. claude-opus-4-6 ). effort enum Override effort level: low | medium | high | xhigh | max . Overrides session default ( high for Pro/Max on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6; medium otherwise). context string Set to fork to run in isolated subagent context with fresh context window. As of v2.1.218, fork-context skills run in the background by default. background boolean Controls whether a context: fork skill runs in the background. Defaults to true for fork skills (v2.1.218). Set to false to opt out and keep the skill in the foreground. agent string Subagent type when context: fork (e.g. Explore , Plan ). hooks object Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.). Also fires when the agent is run as a main-thread agent via --agent . mcpServers object MCP server definitions scoped to this skill. Loaded for fork-subagent contexts and for main-thread agent sessions via --agent . monitors array Background monitor definitions that auto-arm at session start or when the skill is invoked. Enables plugins to stream events without blocking the conversation. Note: in plugin manifest.json files, declare as "experimental": { "monitors": [...] } — top-level still works but triggers a claude plugin validate warning. paths string/list Glob patterns limiting when skill auto-triggers (e.g. src/**/*.ts ). String substitutions: $ARGUMENTS (all args), $0 / $1 (specific args), ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} (skill directory), ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} (session ID), ${CLAUDE_EFFORT} (current effort level — lets a skill branch on low / medium / high / xhigh / max ). Use \$ to include a literal $ before a digit (e.g. \$1 in generated shell scripts) without triggering argument substitution. Frontmatter key casing (v2.1.186): display-name , default-enabled , fallback , and metadata.* keys accept kebab-case, snake_case, or camelCase spellings interchangeably (e.g. display-name , display_name , and displayName are all valid). Malformed YAML frontmatter now loads the skill body with empty metadata instead of failing silently. Boolean values (v2.1.218): Frontmatter boolean fields (e.g., disable-model-invocation , user-invocable ) accept yes / no , on / off , and 1 / 0 (case-insensitive) in addition to true / false . Agent name constraint (v2.1.218): Agent name values in .claude/agents/*.md must not contain : — the colon is reserved for plugin namespacing (e.g., plugin:agent-name ). Files with a colon in the agent name field will be rejected at load time. Project-Level .claude/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md Committed to repo. Shared with team. Global ~/.claude/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md Personal. Available across all projects. Plugin Skills Installed via /plugin . Namespaced as /plugin:skill-name . Priority order: managed (enterprise) > user (global) > project > plugin Nested skill directories: Skills in nested .claude/skills/ directories load automatically when you're working on files in that subdirectory. On a name clash with a parent-scope skill, the nested skill appears as <dir>:<name> so both remain available (v2.1.178). Stacked skill invocations (v2.1.199): Prefix a prompt with multiple slash commands to load all of them — /skill-a /skill-b do XYZ loads both skill-a and skill-b before handing off to Claude. Up to 5 leading skills are loaded in order. Useful for chaining context across a single turn (e.g., /fsd:plan /fsd:code-review-team audit the diff ). Hardened skills synced from claude.ai (v2.1.228): skills synced down from claude.ai no longer shadow local commands or MCP prompts, their descriptions are sanitized and labeled so you can tell them apart from local skills, and on your machine their bodies can't run ! shell commands or expand @ file references. Skill Invocation Manual Type /skill-name [args] to invoke explicitly. Arguments available via $ARGUMENTS , $0 , $1 . Automatic Claude matches your task to skill descriptions and auto-loads the relevant skill. Control with disable-model-invocation . Programmatic Subagents and API integrations invoke skills via the Skill tool. Claude itself can also discover and invoke built-in commands (like /init , /review , /security-review ) this way. Skills can also run in isolated context with context: fork . Auto-Invocation Tip Front-load your description with the key use case in the first 50 characters. Claude uses this to decide when to auto-load the skill. Vague descriptions = poor triggering. Example Skills Documentation Skill ▼ Auto-generates project documentation from codebase analysis. --- name: generate-docs description: Generate project documentation from codebase analysis argument-hint: [module-or-directory] allowed-tools: Read Grep Glob --- # Documentation Generator ## Process 1. Read CLAUDE.md and architecture docs 2. Scan src/ for all public APIs and exported functions 3. For each module: - Extract function signatures and types - Read inline comments and JSDoc - Generate usage examples 4. Create docs/api-reference.md with: - Module index - Function signatures with descriptions - Code examples 5. Verify all links resolve correctly Story Point Estimation Skill ▼ Estimates story points using Fibonacci scale based on complexity analysis. --- name: estimate description: Estimate story points for tasks using Fibonacci scale --- # Story Point Estimation ## Scale - 1: Trivial change, single file, < 30 min - 2: Small change, 2-3 files, < 2 hours - 3: Moderate, multiple files, half day - 5: Significant, cross-module, full day - 8: Large, architectural impact, 2-3 days - 13: Epic-sized, needs decomposition ## Process 1. Read the task/story description 2. Identify affected files and modules 3. Assess: complexity, unknowns, dependencies, risk 4. Compare to reference stories if available 5. Provide estimate with reasoning: - Complexity factors - Risk factors - Suggested decomposition if > 8 points Epic to Stories Skill ▼ Breaks down epics into implementable user stories with acceptance criteria. --- name: epic-to-stories description: Break down epics into implementable user stories --- # Epic Decomposition ## Process 1. Read the epic description and acceptance criteria 2. Identify distinct user capabilities needed 3. For each capability, create a story: - Title: "As a [role], I can [action]" - Description: What and why - Acceptance criteria: Testable, specific - Dependencies: Which stories must complete first 4. Order stories by dependency graph 5. Flag stories that need design input 6. Estimate each story using Fibonacci scale ## Output Format For each story: ### Story [N]: [Title] **As a** [role] **I can** [action] **so that** [value] **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] Criterion 1 - [ ] Criterion 2 **Dependencies:** [Story refs] **Estimate:** [points] Code Review Skill ▼ Structured code review with security, performance, and style checks. --- name : code-review description : Structured code review for PRs and code changes disable-model-invocation : true allowed-tools : Read Grep Glob --- # Code Review ## Security (Critical — block merge if failed) - [ ] No SQL injection vectors - [ ] No XSS vulnerabilities - [ ] No secrets/credentials in code - [ ] Input validation on all external boundaries - [ ] Auth checks on all protected routes ## Logic - [ ] Edge cases handled - [ ] Error handling is appropriate (not swallowed) - [ ] No race conditions in async code - [ ] Data validation matches schema ## Quality - [ ] Tests cover new code paths - [ ] No dead code introduced - [ ] Naming follows project conventions - [ ] No unnecessary complexity ## Output Provide: ✅ Approve, 🔄 Request Changes, or 🚫 Block With specific line-level feedback for each issue. Advanced Skill Patterns ▼ Shell injection — embed live data in skills with !`command` syntax: --- name: pr-summary description: Summarize the current PR diff and comments disable-model-invocation: true --- PR diff: !`gh pr diff` Comments: !`gh pr view --comments` Summarize the changes and highlight any concerns. Context fork — run a skill in an isolated subagent context: --- name: security-audit description: Audit codebase for security vulnerabilities context: fork agent: Explore --- Audit $ARGUMENTS for: 1. Injection vulnerabilities 2. Authentication bypasses 3. Data exposure risks Tool pre-approval — skip permission prompts for expected operations: allowed-tools: Read Grep Bash(git *) Bash(npm test) Extended thinking — include "ultrathink" in skill content to enable deep reasoning. Supporting files — organize templates, scripts, and reference docs alongside SKILL.md. Access the skill's directory with ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} . Creating Skills with the Skill Creator You don't have to write skills from scratch. Claude's built-in skill creator walks you through the process interactively. 1 Run the Skill Creator Launch the interactive skill creator from any Claude Code session. /skill-creator 2 Describe What You Want Tell Claude what workflow to encode. Be specific about the domain and the outcome you want. The more context you provide, the better the skill. "Create a skill for our staging deployment checklist — it should verify tests pass, check environment variables, run database migrations, deploy to staging, and run smoke tests against the staging URL." 3 Iterate on the Draft Claude generates a skill file and walks you through it. Review each section — refine the steps, add edge cases, tighten the checklist. Treat it like a code review. Tip Paste existing runbooks, wiki pages, or checklists into the conversation. Claude will extract the workflow and structure it as a skill automatically. 4 Save and Test The skill creator saves the directory to .claude/skills/ . Test it immediately by invoking the slash command. # Your new skill is ready to use /deploy-staging # List all available skills /skills # Iterate on changes without restarting /reload-plugins 5 Share with Your Team Commit project-level skills to the repo so every teammate gets them automatically. Keep personal utilities in your global skills folder. Project-Level (Shared) .claude/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md Committed to repo. Whole team benefits. Global (Personal) ~/.claude/skills/my-utils/SKILL.md Available across all your projects. Skills vs Commands vs Agents Type What It Is When to Use Skill Markdown directory with SKILL.md . Loaded on demand or auto-invoked. Reusable workflows, checklists, domain knowledge. The default choice. Agent Isolated worker with its own context window and tool access. Parallel work, research, tasks that need context isolation. Command (legacy) File in .claude/commands/ . Replaced by skills. Migrate to .claude/skills/ — commands still work but skills are the standard. Skills can run in agent context with context: fork — giving you the reusability of skills with the isolation of agents. Best Practice Start with one skill for your most repeated workflow. Add more as patterns emerge. A team of 3-4 engineers typically needs 5-8 shared skills to cover their common workflows.

Data exposure risks Tool pre-approval — skip permission prompts for expected operations: allowed-tools: Read Grep Bash(git *) Bash(npm test) Extended thinking — include "ultrathink" in skill content to enable deep reasoning. Supporting files — organize templates, scripts, and reference docs alongside SKILL.md. Access the skill's directory with ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} .

title: Lessons from Real-World FSAD Adoption
label: 12 — Best Practices & Guidelines
text: 12 — Best Practices & Guidelines Lessons from Real-World FSAD Adoption Practical guidance for teams adopting spec-driven agentic development. Background Context Matters Avoid over-emphasis on technical capabilities. Insufficient business context hurts initial coding sessions. A holistic approach beyond engineering-only specifications yields best results. Include background details, business context, problems to be solved, and design systems. Prompting Be Specific About What, Not How Tell Claude what outcome you want, not the implementation steps. Let the agent choose the approach based on codebase context. Provide Business Context Include business requirements, constraints, and existing patterns. "We need a user preferences API because mobile users complain about notification noise" is better than "add a PATCH endpoint." Use @ References Point Claude at specific files with @filename . This ensures the right context is loaded and prevents the agent from searching in the wrong places. Use Plan Mode First For complex features, start with --conversation-mode plan . Let Claude analyze and propose before making changes. Review the plan, then execute. Project Structure Keep CLAUDE.md Concise Under 100 lines. If it's too long, Claude may miss critical rules. Move detailed docs to docs/ for progressive loading. Use Local CLAUDE.md Files Place module-specific rules near the code they protect. src/auth/CLAUDE.md gets loaded when Claude works in that directory. Organize docs/ for Progressive Context Architecture overview, ADRs, and runbooks in docs/ . Claude reads them when relevant, not every session. Version Control Your Prompts Specs, skills, and configuration are code. Commit them. Review changes in PRs. Roll back if something breaks. Workflow Use /clear Between Tasks Reset context between unrelated tasks. Stale context from a previous task can mislead agents on the current one. Use /compact When Context Gets Large Compress conversation history to free up context window space for the current task. Especially useful in long sessions. Commit Frequently Small, atomic changes. Each commit should represent one logical unit of work. Makes it easy to revert if an agent goes off track. Review Agent Output Before Shipping Agents produce consistent code from specs, but they can hallucinate or over-interpret. Human review is non-negotiable. Todo Tools Are Opt-In on Newer Models TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList, and TodoWrite are no longer available by default on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and newer models (v2.1.233). Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 to restore them. Common Pitfalls Jumping Straight to Code Without a spec, agents guess at requirements. The result is wasted cycles and code that doesn't match what was needed. Technical Specs Without Business Context "Add a PATCH endpoint" tells the agent what to build but not why. Missing context leads to wrong trade-offs. Not Using Plan Mode For complex features, jumping straight to implementation means no opportunity to catch misunderstandings before they become code. Ignoring Context Window Limits Overloading a session with too many files or too large a scope causes the agent to lose track of requirements mid-task. Not Reviewing Agent Code Agents are powerful but non-deterministic. Code that passes tests can still have logic errors, security gaps, or architectural drift. Bloated CLAUDE.md Stuffing every rule into CLAUDE.md defeats the purpose. Keep it focused on high-level rules; use docs/ and local CLAUDE.md for details.

title: Model & Effort
label: 12.5 — Model & Effort
text: 12.5 — Model & Effort Model & Effort Pick the right model tier for the task, combine them with opusplan , and tune reasoning depth with /effort . Match model capability to task complexity. Claude Code auto-selects a sensible default, but the best coding results in 2026 come from combining all three tiers — not picking one for everything. Current model lineup Capability Fable 5 New Opus 5 New Opus 4.8 Opus 4.7 Sonnet 4.6 Haiku 4.5 Positioning Mythos-class — most capable model ever made generally available Next-gen Opus — 1M context, fast mode; now default opus alias (v2.1.219) Frontier reasoning, agentic coding, long-horizon autonomy Frontier reasoning + agentic coding Balanced daily driver Fast, near-frontier API ID claude-fable-5 claude-opus-5 claude-opus-4-8 claude-opus-4-7 claude-sonnet-4-6 claude-haiku-4-5 Input / Output (per MTok) See docs $10 / $50 (fast mode) $5 / $25 $5 / $25 $3 / $15 $1 / $5 Context window See docs 1M tokens 1M tokens 1M tokens 1M tokens 200K tokens Max output See docs See docs 128K 128K 64K 64K Adaptive thinking Yes Yes Yes (default high ) Yes (default xhigh ) Yes No (extended thinking only) Relative latency See docs See docs Moderate Moderate Fast Fastest Best for Highest-stakes reasoning, frontier capability tasks, architecture, RCA Complex reasoning, architecture, gnarly bugs — when Fable 5 is over-budget Long-horizon agentic coding, multi-day projects, computer-use, architecture Long-horizon agentic coding, large refactors, architecture, RCA 80%+ of day-to-day coding, tests, tool use Sub-agent work, batch reviews, mechanical edits Claude Code model aliases Alias Resolves to When to use default Tier-dependent (Max / Team Premium → Opus 4.8; Pro / Team Std / Enterprise / API → Sonnet 5; Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry → Opus 4.8) Daily driver if unsure fable Claude Fable 5 ( claude-fable-5 ) — Mythos-class frontier model (v2.1.170+). Includes 1M context by default — fable[1m] suffix is redundant and stripped automatically (v2.1.173) Highest-stakes reasoning, frontier capability tasks best / opus Claude Opus 5 ( claude-opus-5 ) — now the default Opus model (v2.1.219). 1M context window; fast mode at $10/$50 per MTok. Previously resolved to Opus 4.8. Complex reasoning, architecture, gnarly bugs sonnet Claude Sonnet 5 — now the default Claude Code model (v2.1.197). Native 1M-token context window; promotional pricing $2/$10 per MTok through August 31, 2026. (4.5 on Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry) 80%+ of coding tasks; daily driver haiku Latest Haiku Cheap sub-agent / background work opus[1m] / sonnet[1m] 1M context variant Long-session work across large codebases opusplan Opus during plan mode → Sonnet during execution Recommended default for non-trivial feature work — ~40% cheaper than pure Opus # Recommended: let Opus plan, Sonnet execute claude --model opusplan # Force a specific model mid-session /model opus # Switch to latest Opus /model sonnet # Switch to latest Sonnet /model haiku # Switch to latest Haiku /model opus[1m] # 1M context variant for large codebases # Route sub-agents to Haiku (single biggest cost lever after opusplan) — sets the default only; an agent's own model: frontmatter or an explicit per-spawn model overrides it (v2.1.251) export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku # Set the default model for new sessions (v2.1.236) — a /model pick still overrides it and persists across restarts, unlike ANTHROPIC_MODEL export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL=sonnet # Set effort level (controls reasoning depth) /effort max # Maximum reasoning — complex agentic tasks /effort xhigh # Opus 4.7 / 4.8 — between high and max /effort high # Deep thinking — difficult coding problems /effort medium # Balanced (default) — speed + quality /effort low # Quick responses — simple tasks, subagents /effort # No args: opens interactive slider (arrow keys + Enter) claude --effort max # Set via CLI flag # Toggle fast mode (same model, faster output) /fast on # Auto-fallback when primary model not found (interactive + print mode) claude -p --fallback-model sonnet "query" Best-practice combinations by workload Workload Plan Execute Sub-agents Greenfield feature, multi-file Opus 4.8 ( xhigh ) Sonnet 4.6 Haiku 4.5 Targeted bug fix (known file) Sonnet 4.6 Sonnet 4.6 Haiku 4.5 Architectural refactor (10+ files) Opus 4.8 ( max , one-shot) Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 4.6 Haiku 4.5 Boilerplate / rename / formatting — Haiku 4.5 — High-volume code review / lint triage — Haiku 4.5 (Batch API) — Long-session monorepo exploration Opus 4.8 [1m] or Sonnet [1m] Sonnet 4.6 [1m] Haiku 4.5 Production incident / RCA Opus 4.8 ( max ) Opus 4.8 Sonnet 4.6 Cost Optimization Checklist Default to opusplan for coding — ~40% cheaper than pure Opus. Route sub-agents to Haiku via CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku — sets the default only; an agent's own model: frontmatter or an explicit per-spawn model takes precedence (v2.1.251). Enable prompt caching — cache hits are 10% of base input (up to 90% off on repeated system prompts, CLAUDE.md, large docs). Use the Batch API for any non-interactive job — 50% off input and output; stacks with caching. Pin effort to medium on cost-sensitive Sonnet workflows; raise only where needed. Budget for up to 35% more tokens when migrating from Opus 4.6 → 4.7 (new tokenizer). Key Dates (Apr–Jul 2026) July 25, 2026 — Claude Opus 5 released ( claude-opus-5 ). Now the default opus alias target. 1M context window; fast mode pricing at $10/$50 per MTok. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219+. June 9, 2026 — Claude Fable 5 released ( claude-fable-5 ). Mythos-class model — "capabilities exceed those of any model we've ever made generally available." Update Claude Code to v2.1.170 for access. Announcement → May 28, 2026 — Opus 4.8 released ( claude-opus-4-8 ). Available on API, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry. Defaults to high effort on all surfaces. April 23, 2026 — Default model for Enterprise PAYG + Anthropic API switched to Opus 4.7 (now superseded by Opus 4.8). June 15, 2026 — Sonnet 4 ( claude-sonnet-4-20250514 ) and Opus 4 ( claude-opus-4-20250514 ) retire. Migrate to Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8. On Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry, pin model versions explicitly ( ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL , etc.) — alias targets move under you. Default Effort by Model Opus 4.8 defaults to high on all surfaces — API, Claude Code, and all cloud deployments. Pro and Max subscribers on Sonnet 4.6 or Opus 4.7 / 4.6 also default to high . All other tiers and models default to medium . The setting is sticky — it persists across sessions. For complex agentic work, architecture decisions, and multi-file changes, use /effort max . If you've changed effort previously, verify you're on the latest Claude Code version and check that your CLAUDE.md and /memory don't have conflicting effort instructions. Adaptive thinking & effort On Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6, adaptive thinking is the recommended mode. Instead of manually setting a thinking token budget, Claude dynamically decides when and how much to think based on task complexity. The /effort level is the primary lever that controls thinking depth: Effort Thinking Behavior max Always thinks, no constraints on depth — deepest reasoning xhigh Opus 4.7 / Opus 4.8 — deeper than high, lighter than max; falls back to high on other models high Almost always thinks — deep reasoning on complex tasks medium Moderate thinking — may skip for simple queries low Minimal thinking — skips for simple tasks, prioritizes speed Toggle extended thinking with Option+T / Alt+T . Setting effort to low effectively minimizes thinking; use this for simple lookups or subagent tasks where speed matters most. budget_tokens Is Deprecated The manual budget_tokens parameter for extended thinking is deprecated on Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6 and will be removed in a future release. Use adaptive thinking with the effort parameter instead. Older models (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5) still require the manual budget_tokens approach.

title: Everything You Need in One Place
label: 13 — Claude Cheat Sheet
text: 13 — Claude Cheat Sheet Everything You Need in One Place Keyboard shortcuts, commands, flags, hooks, and configuration reference. Keyboard Shortcuts Key Action Enter Send message / submit Esc Interrupt / stop generation. In fullscreen mode it no longer clears a mouse text selection — the highlight stays put while Esc interrupts or dismisses as usual. Bind the selection:clear action in ~/.claude/keybindings.json if you want a key that clears it (v2.1.234) Esc Esc Rewind / restore previous state Shift+Tab Cycle permission mode: manual → acceptEdits → plan → auto (v2.1.200: "default" renamed to "manual") Ctrl+L Force screen redraw (does not clear input — readline behavior as of v2.1.126) Ctrl+C Cancel current operation (hard stop) Ctrl+R Search prompt history across all projects (default). Press Ctrl+S to narrow to the current project or session. Ctrl+S Narrow Ctrl+R history picker to the current project or session only Ctrl+T Toggle task list. In claude agents view: pin/unpin the selected background session — pinned sessions stay alive when idle and are restarted in place on Claude Code updates. Ctrl+X In claude agents view: permanently remove a completed session from the list (v2.1.206) Ctrl+O Toggle normal / verbose transcript Ctrl+B Background running tasks Ctrl+D Exit Claude Code Ctrl+G Open prompt in external text editor Tab Accept autocomplete suggestion Option+T / Alt+T Toggle extended thinking mode Option+P / Alt+P Switch model Option+O / Alt+O Toggle fast mode Ctrl+V / Cmd+V Paste image (screenshots, diagrams) ↑ / ↓ Navigate through command history \ + Enter Multiline input (quick escape) Option+Enter Multiline input (macOS) Space (hold) Push-to-talk voice dictation Ctrl+A / Ctrl+E Jump to start / end of line Ctrl+W Delete word backward. Set keybindingFlavor: "readline" in settings.json to delete back to the previous whitespace instead, as in Bash; the default ( "classic" ) leaves this unchanged (v2.1.238). As of v2.1.239, the same setting also matches Bash for other word keys: Alt+F / Ctrl+→ / Option+→ stop at the end of the word, Alt+D deletes to it ( Ctrl+Y pastes it back), and punctuation now separates words. Ctrl+K Delete from cursor to end of line Ctrl+U Clear entire input buffer (press Ctrl+Y to restore) Slash Commands As of v2.1.236, pressing Enter on a mistyped or unavailable slash command reports the issue instead of silently running the closest fuzzy match; valid prefixes and aliases still run normally. Session, context & history Command Description /compact [focus] Compress context to save tokens. Optional: tell it what to keep. /context Visualize context usage with optimization suggestions. As of v2.1.216, shows an explicit warning when the conversation exceeds the context window; a failed /compact now displays as an error. As of v2.1.235, the context-limit error states when auto-compact is turned off and points to /config to re-enable it. /clear Clear conversation history (aliases: /reset , /new ) /resume [session] Resume conversation by ID or name (alias: /continue ). Offers to summarize stale large sessions before re-reading them. Paste a GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, or Bitbucket PR URL into the search box to jump directly to the session that created that PR. Background sessions started via --bg or agent view now appear in the picker, marked with bg . In the agent view, typing /resume opens a picker that includes sessions previously deleted from the list — deleted sessions remain accessible and resume as a background session (v2.1.212). As of v2.1.243, the picker is no longer capped at the 50 most recent sessions — it loads more as you scroll. /rename [name] Rename session or auto-generate a name /cd <path> Move the session to a new working directory without breaking the prompt cache mid-session (v2.1.169) /add-dir <path> Grant the session access to an additional working directory. As of v2.1.234 it can be run while Claude is working, so a mid-run "needs a directory it doesn't have access to" no longer means interrupting the turn. In the fullscreen TUI, /add-dir , /autocompact , /theme , /help , /config and /advisor all open their dialogs mid-turn (v2.1.234) /recap Replay session context — useful when returning to a long-running session. Configurable in /config . Force on: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY=1 ; opt out: =0 (also disables the default-on behavior on Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry). /rewind Rewind to previous checkpoint (aliases: /undo , /checkpoint ). The Rewind menu also offers Summarize up to here — compress earlier context while preserving recent turns, without rolling back state. As of v2.1.191, the Rewind menu also lets you resume from before a /clear was run, recovering the conversation state that existed before the context was cleared. /export Export conversation to file or clipboard /copy [N] Copy last response to clipboard (or Nth-last) /diff Open interactive diff viewer. In the detail view, scroll with arrow keys, j / k , PgUp / PgDn , Space , Home / End (v2.1.149). /btw Share a side note or correction mid-task without interrupting the model's current turn. Use ←/→ arrows to step through earlier answers (v2.1.187). Model, mode & usage Command Description /model Select or change AI model — selection is saved as the default for new sessions. Press s in the picker to switch models for the current session only. Startup header shows when the active model comes from a project or managed-settings pin. When ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a compatible gateway, set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 to list gateway models in the picker (opt-in as of v2.1.129). As of v2.1.243, the picker no longer silently ignores an Ultracode selection — picking it now applies to the current session. On Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry disabled, /model also now applies immediately instead of queueing until the turn ends. /effort [level] Set effort level: low | medium | high | xhigh (Opus 4.7 / 4.8) | max . Call with no args for interactive slider. Default: high for Opus 4.8 (all surfaces) and Pro/Max on Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.7 / 4.6; medium for all other tiers/models. Confirms when the chosen level will persist as the default for new sessions (v2.1.162). On Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry disabled, /effort now applies immediately instead of queueing until the turn ends (v2.1.243). As of v2.1.251, /effort saves your default effort level per model, so each model keeps its own setting when you switch. /fast [on|off] Toggle fast mode (same model, faster output). On Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry disabled, /fast now applies immediately instead of queueing until the turn ends (v2.1.243). /plan [desc] Enter plan mode with optional starting description /focus Toggle focus view (hides system status lines for a cleaner reading experience) /permissions View & edit tool permissions (alias: /allowed-tools ). As of v2.1.234 it can be opened while Claude is working — rule changes apply to the rest of the current turn, so you can widen or tighten a rule without interrupting a long run (v2.1.234). As of v2.1.246, an Auto mode tab lets you view and edit auto mode classifier rules from the same dialog, instead of editing them only via settings.json . /usage Unified usage dashboard with three tabs: session cost & token usage, plan usage & rate limits, and daily usage streaks. Includes a per-category breakdown showing what's driving limits usage — skills, subagents, plugins, and per-MCP-server cost (v2.1.149). /cost and /stats remain as typing shortcuts that open the relevant tab. As of v2.1.236, /usage also shows a usage-credits spend row for Team and Enterprise members, capped at 0% before any credits have been spent. As of v2.1.239, cost estimates shown via /cost , the status line, and enforced by --max-budget-usd include the 1.1× US-only-inference premium that applies to data-residency workspaces, so the figures reflect actual billed cost. As of v2.1.243, /usage also includes a Loops breakdown — per-loop run count, total tokens, tokens per run, and last run — to spot runaway or chatty /loop tasks. As of v2.1.251, a per-session prompt-cache line is also shown on /cost — hit ratio, misses, tokens re-cached, warm/cold — with a matching prompt_cache object available for status line scripts. /usage-credits View usage credits balance (alias: /extra-usage ). Added in v2.1.144. As of v2.1.248, members of Enterprise organizations billed through AWS Marketplace, self-serve Enterprise, and Enterprise trials can use it to request a higher usage limit from their admin. Automation & agents Command Description /loop [interval] <prompt> Run prompt on recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m check tests ). Alias: /proactive /schedule Create / manage cloud scheduled tasks /batch <instruction> Orchestrate large-scale changes (5–30 parallel agents) /tasks List and manage background tasks (alias: /bashes ). As of v2.1.243, each subagent's row and its detail dialog show the model (and effort level) it ran on. /agents Browse agent library and manage live subagents (Running + Library tabs) /goal <condition> Set a completion condition and Claude works across turns until it's met — shows live elapsed/turns/tokens overlay. Works in interactive, -p , and Remote Control. As of v2.1.234, a goal clears itself with a notice when a turn dies on an unrecoverable error (e.g. revoked auth, an exhausted credit balance, or a context overflow) instead of staying armed, and Claude checks in on background tasks that have kept a goal waiting, on an escalating cadence — 30 minutes, then 1 hour, then 2 hours — rather than waiting indefinitely (v2.1.236; originally a flat 30-minute check-in in v2.1.234) — set CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0 to opt out. As of v2.1.246, an idle goal makes at most three such check-ins before it stops escalating; sending the session a new message allows three more. As of v2.1.239, resuming a session from the claude --resume picker also restores its active goal. /workflows View and manage dynamic workflow runs — Claude orchestrates tens to hundreds of parallel agents to tackle large-scale tasks. Available on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans (v2.1.154). /security-review Analyze pending changes for security issues /dataviz Chart and dashboard design guidance — guides through chart type selection, accessible color formulas (with a runnable palette validator), mark specs, and interaction rules for HTML/React, SVG, and plotting libraries. Use before writing any chart or visualization code (v2.1.198). /fork Copy the current conversation into a new background session (its own row in claude agents ) while you keep working in the original. The former in-session subagent behavior is now /subtask (v2.1.212). As of v2.1.221, the forked session runs in its own new git worktree instead of continuing in the original session's checkout. /subtask Launch an in-session subagent with its own context window — the former /fork behavior (v2.1.212). Configuration & setup Command Description /config [key=value] Open settings interface — or set any setting inline: /config thinking=false , /config model=sonnet . Run /config --help to list all available shorthand keys. Changes persist to ~/.claude/settings.json and participate in the config cascade. Works in interactive, -p , and Remote Control (alias: /settings ) (v2.1.183). As of v2.1.234, Claude Code continues an interrupted session automatically when a claude.ai usage limit resets — useful for long unattended runs. On by default; turn it off with the "Continue automatically at usage limit" toggle in /config (v2.1.234). As of v2.1.237, a built-in "Concise" output style is available: Claude leads with results and skips preamble and narration while doing the work just as thoroughly. Select it under Output style in /config (v2.1.237). /init Create CLAUDE.md for your project /memory Edit CLAUDE.md and manage auto-memory /tui [fullscreen] Switch to fullscreen TUI mode with flicker-free rendering ( /tui fullscreen ) /theme Change color theme: dark | light | auto (match terminal) | or select a named custom theme. Hand-edit JSON files in ~/.claude/themes/ to create themes; plugins can ship themes via a themes/ directory. /color [color] Set prompt-bar color (red, blue, green, purple, etc.); omit the argument to pick a random color /terminal-setup Setup Shift+Enter for multi-line input; also configures scroll sensitivity in VS Code, Cursor, and Devin Desktop terminals; enables iTerm2 clipboard access for /copy (including from tmux) /scroll-speed Tune mouse wheel scroll speed with a live preview /keybindings Open / create keybindings configuration. Actions are bound by name in ~/.claude/keybindings.json — e.g. selection:clear binds a key to clear an in-app text selection, and also works in the agents view (v2.1.234). /doctor Full setup checkup — diagnoses and fixes environment issues. Shows an exec-form example hint when a command hook is missing the command field; lists installed skills and components. Also checks for CLAUDE.md content that Claude could derive from the codebase and proposes trimming it (v2.1.206). Alias: /checkup (v2.1.205). /less-permission-prompts Scan transcripts for common read-only Bash/MCP calls and propose an allowlist for settings.json /sandbox Enable OS-level sandboxing for Bash subprocesses — choose Auto-allow mode (sandboxed commands run without approval prompts) or Regular permissions mode (standard flow, sandbox still enforces boundaries). macOS: built-in via Seatbelt. Linux / WSL2: requires bubblewrap and socat . /mcp Manage MCP server connections; shows tool count per server and flags servers with 0 tools (usually a misconfiguration). As of v2.1.161, claude.ai connectors you have never signed in to are collapsed behind a "Show unused connectors" row to reduce visual noise. CLI alternative (v2.1.186): claude mcp login <name> authenticates an MCP server without opening the interactive menu — useful in CI or SSH sessions; add --no-browser to redirect the OAuth flow to stdin. claude mcp logout <name> clears stored credentials. claude mcp list / claude mcp get now show disabled servers as ⊘ Disabled directly instead of connecting to them for a health check (v2.1.238). As of v2.1.243, claude.ai connectors whose authentication is managed by your organization show a managed marker. /hooks View hook configurations /skills List available skills; type to filter by name in long lists /plugin Manage Claude Code plugins — the marketplace browse and discover panes show a full component preview (commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP/LSP servers), projected per-turn and per-invocation token cost estimates, and when each plugin was last updated — all before you install. A search bar is available when browsing the marketplace to filter plugins by name (v2.1.172). Use claude plugin details <name> for the same inventory from the CLI. Use claude plugin list (with optional --enabled or --disabled filter) to list installed plugins from the CLI. As of v2.1.243, claude.ai connectors whose authentication is managed by your organization show a managed marker. /reload-plugins Reload plugins without restart /reload-skills Re-scan skill directories and reload skills without restarting the session Cross-device & integrations Command Description /remote-control Enable remote control from claude.ai (alias: /rc ) claude remote-control --continue Resume the most recent Remote Control session from the CLI (v2.1.229) /teleport Pull web session into terminal (alias: /tp ) /desktop Continue in Claude Code Desktop app /mobile Show QR code for mobile app (aliases: /ios , /android ) /voice Toggle push-to-talk voice dictation /ide Manage IDE integrations and status /install-github-app Set up automated PR reviews. GitHub Actions workflow/secret setup is optional — you can install just the GitHub App and skip the CI steps (v2.1.187). /install-slack-app Install Claude Slack app Info & account Command Description /help Show help and available commands /status Show session config and token usage metrics. As of v2.1.221, also displays the session kind: interactive , or a background job that is attached or unattended . As of v2.1.243, also shows a Skipped sources line listing managed settings sources (e.g. managed-settings.json ) present but not applied because a higher-precedence managed source is active, and a line showing whether GitHub is connected for Claude Code on the web (Pro/Max) — pointing to /web-setup when it isn't. /release-notes View changelog with version picker /powerup Interactive feature lessons with animated demos /team-onboarding Generate a teammate ramp-up guide from your local Claude Code usage history /ultrareview [PR#] Cloud-based parallel multi-agent code review — omit args for current branch, or pass a GitHub PR number. Also available as claude ultrareview [target] non-interactively from CI/scripts ( --json for raw output; exits 0 on completion, 1 on failure). /deep-research [topic] Fan-out web research harness — launches parallel agents to search, fetch sources, verify claims, and synthesize a cited report on the given topic. As of v2.1.218, only starts when invoked manually; Claude no longer launches it autonomously. /code-review [effort] Run a code review on the current branch as a background subagent — review work no longer fills your active conversation, and stacked slash commands keep the review as their target (v2.1.218). Optionally pass an effort level (e.g., /code-review high ) to override the default. Pass --comment to post findings as inline GitHub PR comments. Pass --fix to automatically apply findings (reuse, simplification, efficiency) to your working tree after review. /simplify runs a cleanup-only review (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) and applies the fixes directly — a lighter alternative to --fix . As of v2.1.215, Claude no longer runs this skill automatically — invoke it explicitly when you want a review. As of v2.1.246, this restriction is lifted on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Foundry, through the Claude apps gateway, and when telemetry or non-essential traffic is disabled — Claude may start a review on its own in these configurations. As of v2.1.223, /review is an alias of /code-review ; pass a PR number to review a pull request instead of the current branch ( /code-review <level> <pr#> ), and /code-review ultra triggers a deep cloud review. Invoking with no effort level now reuses whichever level you last typed instead of falling back to the default. /verify Verify that a code change works as expected by exercising the affected flow end-to-end — observes real behavior rather than relying on tests or typechecks alone. As of v2.1.215, Claude no longer invokes this automatically — call it explicitly to trigger a verification pass (v2.1.215). claude agents Agent View — a unified list of every Claude Code session: running, blocked on you, or done. Use --cwd <path> to scope the list to a directory. Add --json to output the session list as JSON for scripting (tmux-resurrect, status bars, session pickers); blocked and just-dispatched sessions are always included; the JSON output includes waitingFor (what a blocked session is waiting on), id , and state fields (v2.1.162/v2.1.169). Add --all to include completed sessions in the output (v2.1.169). When dispatching a background session, configure it with: --add-dir , --settings , --mcp-config , --plugin-dir , --permission-mode , --model , --effort , --dangerously-skip-permissions . In the agents view, type ! <command> to launch any shell command as a background session you can attach to and detach from (v2.1.154). CLI equivalent: claude --bg --exec '<command>' . When work is fanned out across subagents, each row shows done/total progress counts before the detail; the peek highlights the longest-running item (v2.1.161). Sessions tied to a GitHub PR or GitLab merge request show the PR/MR number in the list — GitLab MRs display as !N (GitLab merge request URL support added v2.1.233). claude project purge [path] Delete all Claude Code state for a project — transcripts, tasks, file history, and config entry. Flags: --dry-run (preview), -y (no confirm), -i/--interactive , --all (all known projects). claude auto-mode reset Restore the default auto-mode configuration. Prompts for confirmation; pass --yes to skip (v2.1.212). claude attach / logs / stop / respawn / rm <id> Manage a background session directly from the shell without opening the agent view: attach to its live output, tail its logs, stop it, respawn it, or remove it from the list. As of v2.1.251, the --resume message for a running background session names the exact claude attach <id> command instead of a generic hint. /insights Generate session analysis report (HTML) /claude-api upgrade Migrate a Python project's use of the anthropic SDK from 0.x to 1.x (v2.1.239) /claude-api cost-optimize Profile a project's existing Claude API spend and work through cost levers — caching, token hygiene, batch, effort, model choice — one measured change at a time (v2.1.247). The /claude-api skill also gained Admin API coverage in v2.1.247 (organization members, invites, workspaces, API keys, rate limit reports, workload identity federation, CMEK). /feedback Review and send a feedback report Claude drafted when something went wrong in the session, via the SendFeedback tool. Turn off with the feedbackDrafts setting (v2.1.247). /login Sign in to Anthropic account. As of v2.1.243, choosing Anthropic Console offers a keyless "Sign in with your Console account" option (recommended) alongside creating an API key — useful for organizations that don't allow API keys. /logout Sign out CLI Launch Flags Session & startup Flag Description claude Start interactive session claude "query" Start with an initial prompt --continue / -c Resume last conversation --resume / -r Resume specific session by ID or name --name / -n Set session display name --fork-session Create new session ID when resuming --worktree / -w Start in isolated git worktree. As of v2.1.233, also accepts a GitLab merge request URL (MRs display as !N ). --tmux Create tmux session with worktree --add-dir Add additional working directories Model & effort Flag Description --model Select specific model ( sonnet , opus , haiku ) --effort Set effort level ( low | medium | high | xhigh | max ).
