Default: high for Opus 4.8 (all surfaces) and Pro/Max on Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.7 / 4.6; medium otherwise. --fallback-model Switch to this model for the rest of the session when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable (interactive and print mode); use the fallbackModel settings key to configure up to three fallbacks tried in order Permissions & tools Flag Description --permission-mode Start in specific mode ( plan , auto , acceptEdits ) --allowedTools Tools that execute without prompting --disallowedTools Tools unavailable to model --dangerously-skip-permissions Skip all permission prompts — including writes to .claude/ , .git/ , .vscode/ , and shell config files. Catastrophic removal commands still prompt as a safety net. CI/CD and trusted automation only. Print / programmatic mode Flag Description -p / --print Print mode — answer & exit (for scripting) --from-pr Load PR/MR diff as context — accepts GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, and Bitbucket URLs --output-format json JSON output --output-format stream-json Streaming JSON output --forward-subagent-text Include subagent text and thinking in stream-json output. As of v2.1.219, nested subagents spawned at depth-2+ are also included, each keyed by their spawning Agent tool_use id — useful for automated pipelines that need full visibility into deeply-nested agentic activity. Env var: CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT=1 (v2.1.211). --json-schema Get JSON output matching a specific schema --max-turns Limit number of agentic turns --max-budget-usd Maximum spend before stopping ($) --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections Strip dynamic prompt sections to enable cross-user prompt cache sharing System prompt & config Flag Description --system-prompt Replace entire system prompt --append-system-prompt Append to the default system prompt --mcp-config Load MCP servers from JSON file --agent Specify agent for session --chrome Enable Chrome browser integration --remote Create web session on claude.ai --channels Enable channels with console (API key) authentication. Console orgs with managed settings must set channelsEnabled: true in org settings to allow this. --plugin-url <url> Fetch a plugin .zip archive from a URL and load it for the current session only --bare Minimal mode — skip auto-discovery --safe-mode Start with all customizations disabled (CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP servers) — useful for troubleshooting. Env var equivalent: CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1 (v2.1.169). --ax-screen-reader Enable screen reader mode — opt-in plain-text rendering optimized for screen readers. Env var equivalent: CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 . Also configurable via "axScreenReader": true in settings.json (v2.1.208). --verbose Enable verbose logging --debug Enable debug logging Permission Modes Default Claude asks permission for every tool use. Safest mode. Good for unfamiliar codebases. Accept Edits Auto-accepts file reads and edits. Still prompts for shell commands. Good middle ground. Plan Mode Read-only. Claude ONLY reads & plans. Won't write or edit files. Perfect for spec creation and analysis. Auto-Accept No prompts. Fastest execution. Use when you trust the agent and want maximum speed. Bypass Permissions Requires --dangerously-skip-permissions flag. Bypasses prompts for .claude/ , .git/ , .vscode/ , and shell config files. Catastrophic removal commands still prompt. CI/CD and trusted automation only. Cycle with Shift+Tab : default → acceptEdits → plan → auto → (bypassPermissions if enabled) Hooks — Event Automation (30 Events) Core hooks Hook When It Fires SessionStart When a session begins or resumes. Return reloadSkills: true in JSON output to re-scan skill directories (skills installed by the hook become available immediately). Set session title via hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle . Hook input includes a source field: "new" (first launch), "resume" (resumed session), or "fork" (started via /fork — v2.1.214). As of v2.1.251, resume hooks also receive the session's staleness and the estimated re-cache cost. SessionEnd When a session ends InstructionsLoaded After CLAUDE.md and settings are loaded UserPromptSubmit Before your message is processed Stop When Claude finishes its complete response. Hook input includes background_tasks and session_crons fields listing active background work and scheduled crons. Return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext in hook JSON output to inject context for Claude and continue the turn without a hook error. StopFailure When Claude's response fails MessageDisplay Before assistant message text is displayed — hooks can transform or hide the output Tool & permission hooks Hook When It Fires PreToolUse Before EVERY tool use — check, audit, intercept PostToolUse After EVERY tool use — lint, format, auto-fix PostToolUseFailure After a tool call fails PermissionRequest When a permission prompt is shown PermissionDenied After a permission is denied in auto mode Agent & task hooks Hook When It Fires SubagentStart When a subagent is spawned SubagentStop When a subagent finishes. Hook input includes background_tasks and session_crons fields. Return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext to give Claude feedback and keep the turn going without a hook error. TaskCreated When a task is created via TaskCreate TaskCompleted When a task finishes TeammateIdle When a teammate agent is idle Environment & context hooks Hook When It Fires ConfigChange When settings or config changes CwdChanged When the working directory changes PreModelSwitch Before a model switch — block, confirm, or annotate the switch (v2.1.251) PostModelSwitch After a model switch completes (v2.1.251) DirectoryAdded When a new working directory is registered mid-session — fires after /add-dir or the SDK register_repo_root control request adds a new repo root (v2.1.219). FileChanged When a file is modified WorktreeCreate When a git worktree is created WorktreeRemove When a git worktree is removed PreCompact Before context compaction PostCompact After context compaction Elicitation When an MCP elicitation dialog is shown ElicitationResult After an MCP elicitation completes Notification When a notification event fires Input Superpowers @mention Type @ to reference files, folders, or named subagents. Claude includes file contents automatically. /commands Type / for slash command and skill autocomplete. !bash Type ! to run a shell command directly from the prompt (e.g. ! git status ). Paste Images Ctrl+V / Cmd+V to paste screenshots, diagrams, error messages directly. Pipe Input cat error.log | claude "fix this" — pipe stdout directly to Claude. Multi-Dir claude --add-dir src/ --add-dir tests/ — work across multiple directories. Voice Hold Space for push-to-talk voice dictation. Supports 20+ languages. Background Ctrl+B backgrounds running tasks so you can start another. File Structure Map PROJECT (.claude/) ├── CLAUDE.md # Project instructions ├── settings.json # Shared project settings ├── rules/ # Path-scoped rules ├── commands/ # Custom slash commands ├── skills/ # Reusable expert modes └── agents/ # Project sub-agents GLOBAL (~/.claude/) ├── CLAUDE.md # Global instructions ├── settings.json # Personal settings ├── commands/ # Personal global commands ├── skills/ # Personal global skills ├── todos/ # Task management ├── keybindings.json # Custom keybindings └── plugins/ # Installed plugins Quick Reference — Most Used Combos Action Command Start project cd project && claude Continue where I left off claude -c Resume named session claude -r my-feature Quick question, no session claude -p "how do I..." Review & fix this file claude "review @file.ts" Explore error cat error.log | claude -p "fix" Parallel sessions claude -w (each gets own worktree) Force model claude --model opus Set effort level /effort max (complex work), /effort xhigh (Opus 4.7 / 4.8), or /effort for interactive slider Remote control from web /remote-control or claude --remote Voice dictation /voice then hold Space to talk Scriptable automation claude -p --output-format json "task"

title: Advanced Features for Power Users
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: 14 — Claude Power Usage Advanced Features for Power Users Agent teams, worktrees, remote control, batch operations, voice, plugins, and more. Agent Teams ▼ Multiple Claude instances collaborating on the same codebase. Each agent works independently with its own context, but they share the same repo and can coordinate through files. Frontend + backend agents working in parallel Writer + reviewer pattern: one implements, another reviews Research agent gathers context while implementation agent builds Nested sub-agents: sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents, enabling hierarchical architectures like orchestrator → specialist → worker trees. Nesting is disabled by default as of v2.1.217 — set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=2 (or higher) to allow it; max depth was 5 levels in earlier versions (v2.1.172, updated v2.1.217) Subagent forking: as of v2.1.232, forking is on by default — a subagent_type: "fork" subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache from its parent instead of starting fresh, and non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now also run in the background by default. Cross-session SendMessage : as of v2.1.224, Claude Code sessions can message each other across any of your machines — not just teammates in the same tmux/worktree setup. Use ListAgents to discover reachable sessions. As of v2.1.225, you can start a conversation with a Remote Control session on another machine by name, instead of only replying after it messages you first — ListAgents shows Remote Control sessions as name [ref] . As of v2.1.228, cross-session messages display the sender and body inline, and messages to Remote Control sessions show your Remote Control session name as the sender. As of v2.1.232, typing @ in the prompt to mention any live session by name (not just teammates) resolves through SendMessage automatically, delivery to a bare name matching exactly one live session no longer waits for ref confirmation, and a session started or renamed to a name already in use on that machine gets a unique name-word-word variant automatically. As of v2.1.234, ListAgents and SendMessage report when your account's session list was too long to enumerate completely, so an unseen session is no longer silently treated as absent — a failed lookup is now distinguishable from a genuinely missing session. As of v2.1.235, SendMessage refuses a message too large for cross-session delivery up front, rather than accepting it and silently dropping it. As of v2.1.236, SendMessage accepts a notify_when_idle option: ask another Claude Code session on this machine to send one notice when it next goes idle — opt-in, one-shot, no polling (macOS and Linux). Available on macOS and Linux. As of v2.1.238, ListAgents and SendMessage now correctly list and reach Remote Control peers from server-mode ( claude remote-control ) and Desktop/IDE-hosted sessions instead of reporting "Remote Control is not connected", no longer expose the idle worker pre-warmed for your next background session until a task claims it, and report a refusal or dropped-inbox failure back to the sender instead of a silent success or a message vanishing. As of v2.1.239, cross-session messaging is available on Windows, reaching parity with macOS and Linux — Windows sessions can message each other with SendMessage and discover each other with ListAgents . ListAgents and /list-agents now correctly include your live teammates in the listing (previously only subagents and other sessions appeared, making a reachable teammate look absent). ListAgents also now tells a session its own addressable name, and SendMessage to your own name reports that instead of "no agent named …". As of v2.1.247, cross-session peer messages collapse by default to a one-line Message from @<sender>: <first line> preview; press Ctrl+O to expand the full body. As of v2.1.248, cross-session messaging ( SendMessage / ListAgents ) between sessions on the same machine is available on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry is disabled — previously limited to direct Anthropic API sessions. Also as of v2.1.248, when a subagent calls SendMessage to another session, any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to the subagent — worth knowing when a subagent-initiated cross-session conversation needs a response the subagent itself won't see. # Spawn a teammate in its own worktree + tmux pane claude -w feature-auth --tmux # Or run teammates in-process (no tmux needed) claude --teammate-mode in-process # Reference named agents with @ in your prompt # Team leader's model and permissions cascade to teammates # Message another running session by name/id SendMessage (to: "<agent-name-or-id>" , ...) # Discover reachable sessions across machines ListAgents () 🔗 Agent Teams Documentation Official docs on configuring and using agent teams Work Trees ▼ Isolated git worktrees for parallel work. Each agent gets its own branch and working directory. Changes merge back when complete. # Start Claude in a new worktree claude -w feature-name # Pair with tmux for side-by-side terminals claude -w feature-name --tmux # Each worktree is a full repo checkout # Agents can work simultaneously without conflicts # Changes are merged back via standard git merge/PR worktree.baseRef setting — controls the branch base for all worktrees ( --worktree , EnterWorktree , and agent-isolation worktrees). Set in .claude/settings.json : Value Branches from When to use fresh (default) origin/<default-branch> Clean base — agents always start from the canonical remote state, no local noise head Local HEAD Share unpushed scaffolding — spawned agents inherit commits you haven't pushed yet worktree.bgIsolation setting — controls whether background sessions run in an isolated worktree or edit the working copy directly. Set in .claude/settings.json : Value Behavior When to use worktree (default) Background sessions run in an isolated git worktree via EnterWorktree Most repos — prevents conflicts with your working copy none Background sessions edit the working copy directly, no worktree created Monorepos with non-relocatable build artifacts or tools that cannot run from a worktree path Tip Worktrees are automatically cleaned up when the agent completes with no changes. If changes were made, the worktree path and branch are returned. WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks fire on lifecycle events. As of v2.1.157, EnterWorktree can switch between Claude-managed worktrees mid-session — an agent can hop from one task-worktree to another without stopping and restarting. As of v2.1.161, parallel tool calls are independent — a failed Bash command no longer cancels other calls in the same batch; each tool returns its own result. As of v2.1.211, "always allow" permission grants are saved at the repository root — approvals made inside a worktree persist across all sessions and worktrees for that repo. As of v2.1.221, background sessions commit and push to preserve their work, open a draft PR only when the task calls for one, follow your CLAUDE.md git instructions, and always end by reporting where the work lives. As of v2.1.238, worktree-isolation Bash refusals no longer tell you to remove a redirect when the command had none. Hooks ▼ Hooks are event-driven shell commands, HTTP endpoints, prompts, or agents that fire automatically at 26 lifecycle points. Use them for linting, formatting, security enforcement, and observability. Hooks Deep Dive See the dedicated Hooks section for the full lifecycle, all 5 hook types, configuration guide, exit code semantics, and practical recipes. Session Logs ▼ Review what Claude did in past sessions. Useful for auditing agent behavior and learning from successful patterns. Location: ~/.claude/projects/ (session transcripts) Each session is logged with timestamps Includes tool calls, file changes, and conversation flow Useful for debugging "what did the agent do while I was away?" Use /export to save a conversation to file or clipboard Press Ctrl+O to toggle normal / verbose transcript; use /focus to toggle focus view /insights — Workflow Analysis ▼ Generates a local HTML report analyzing your last 30 days of coding sessions. Report location: ~/.claude/usage-data/report.html Identifies workflow friction and recurring patterns Actionable feedback on prompting effectiveness Tracks which tools and models you use most # Just type in Claude: /insights # Opens a local HTML report in your browser /loop — Built-in Scheduler (alias: /proactive) ▼ Run commands on a recurring basis. Session-scoped — terminal must stay active. # Check for new issues every hour /loop 1h check for new Git issues and triage them # Run tests every 30 minutes and fix failures /loop 30m check if the codebase passes all tests, if not, fix it # Monitor deployment status /loop 15m check the deploy pipeline status and notify me of failures Cancel a Wakeup Press Esc while a /loop is counting down to cancel the pending wakeup without ending the session. For Persistence Session-scoped loops stop when the terminal closes. For persistent cloud scheduling, use /schedule to create cron-based tasks that run without an active terminal. Monitor Loop Cost /usage has a dedicated Loops breakdown (per-loop run count, total tokens, tokens per run, last run) as of v2.1.243 — check it if a /loop task seems to be running more often or costing more than expected. Available Everywhere Self-paced dynamic mode (no fixed interval — Claude paces itself) and the no-prompt autonomous default are now always available for /loop , including on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (v2.1.248). Dynamic Workflows — Parallel Multi-Agent Orchestration ▼ Dynamic workflows run tens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session — tackling problems too large for a single-pass solution. Claude decomposes the prompt, distributes subtasks across agents working simultaneously, verifies results through independent checking and adversarial refutation, and iterates until answers converge. "Work you'd normally plan in quarters now finishes in days." # Ask Claude directly to create a workflow "Create a workflow to find all security vulnerabilities across the codebase" "Create a workflow to migrate all API calls from v1 to v2" # Or enable ultracode — Claude decides when to use workflows automatically /effort ultracode Best-fit use cases Category Examples Codebase analysis Bug hunts, security audits, optimization reviews across entire services Large migrations Framework swaps, API deprecations, language ports spanning thousands of files Critical validation Independent multi-angle attempts when wrong answers carry high costs Token Cost Dynamic workflows can consume substantially more tokens than a typical Claude Code session. Available on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans . On Enterprise, off by default at launch — admins enable via Claude Code settings. Trigger keyword: ultracode Type the word ultracode in the prompt input (it highlights violet) to let Claude decide when to run a full dynamic workflow automatically. Press Alt+W or Backspace immediately after the keyword appears to dismiss an accidental trigger. To disable the keyword entirely, go to /config → Workflow keyword trigger . (v2.1.160) The built-in workflow prompt keyword uses a purple shimmer highlight and only fires on explicit phrases like "run a workflow" or "workflow:" — casual mentions of "workflow" in conversation no longer trigger it, reducing accidental activations (v2.1.178). Fan-outs now stagger same-prefix sibling agents so later agents read the cached prompt prefix instead of re-paying it, cutting redundant token cost across large parallel dispatches. Set CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS=0 to disable the staggering (v2.1.229). Remote Control & Cross-Device ▼ Control your terminal Claude session from the web, or move sessions between devices seamlessly. # Enable remote control from claude.ai /remote-control /remote-control "My Project" # With custom name # Create a web session directly claude --remote "Fix the login bug" # Pull a web session into your terminal /teleport /desktop — continue session in the Claude Code desktop app (macOS/Windows) /mobile — show QR code to continue on mobile Bridge sessions display your local git repo, branch, and working directory When enabled, Remote Control appears as a persistent footer pill with a direct link to the session — accessible at any time without scrolling back through startup messages (v2.1.162) Photos attached from the Claude mobile app are shown to Claude directly, instead of being read from disk via a separate tool call — faster and more reliable for mobile-initiated sessions (v2.1.225) Session state now syncs in both directions: an effort level picked on a phone or on claude.ai/code applies to the terminal- or Desktop/VS Code-hosted session, and that session publishes its effort level back to connected clients. Sessions started from Claude Code Desktop or VS Code also keep phones and claude.ai/code updated on the session's permission mode as it changes, and claude.ai/code on the model (v2.1.234) Signing this computer in to a different claude.ai account or organization now stops a running Remote Control session within seconds and says why, instead of surfacing a misleading HTTP 404 hours later (v2.1.234) claude rc applies the same enterprise-gateway availability check as interactive startup (v2.1.235) Brief HTTP 403 refusals from a network edge, VPN, or proxy are now tolerated for up to 3 minutes before Remote Control surfaces an error, and the refusing party is named if the block persists (v2.1.238) Remote Control sessions started by claude remote-control no longer inherit session-scoped environment variables from the launching shell; a session whose process crashed can now be reused the next time you message it instead of staying unavailable until claude remote-control is restarted; messages sent from the web or Desktop mid-turn no longer disappear from the transcript once the turn finishes; model picks made on a phone or web now update the model shown in the terminal; a brief network hiccup delaying sign-in renewal no longer disconnects the session with "login expired"; and signing out now ends the session with a clear message instead of reporting a failed reconnect (v2.1.238) A foreground subagent's tool calls and results now stream live to Remote Control clients as they happen — background subagents, the default, still show status only (v2.1.251) Self-Hosted Runner ▼ claude self-hosted-runner turns your own machines or containers into a place Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions can run — an alternative to Anthropic-hosted Managed Web Agents for teams that need sessions to execute on infrastructure they control (data residency, network access to internal systems, custom hardware). Available on Team and Enterprise plans (v2.1.224). # Register this machine/container as a runner claude self-hosted-runner # Drain gracefully on SIGTERM, then park and exit after N minutes (v2.1.238) claude self-hosted-runner --defer-shutdown-max-min 10 # Freshly minted Proxy-Authorization header per connection, via --proxy-authorization-command or --proxy-authorization-file (v2.1.238) claude self-hosted-runner --proxy-authorization-command "..." # Override the registered runner label instead of using the hostname (v2.1.248) claude self-hosted-runner --client-label "ci-runner-3" Once registered, web, mobile, and desktop sessions started by your org can be scheduled onto the runner instead of Anthropic-hosted infrastructure. Chrome Integration ▼ Claude can interact with web pages in a Chrome browser — navigate, fill forms, click buttons, extract data, and take screenshots. # Enable Chrome integration claude --chrome # Or configure via slash command /chrome # Disable when not needed claude --no-chrome Use Cases Debug frontend issues by viewing the page directly, verify UI changes after edits, scrape documentation, or test form flows end-to-end. Batch Operations ▼ Orchestrate large-scale changes across your entire codebase with 5–30 parallel agents working simultaneously. # Rename a function across the entire codebase /batch rename all instances of getUserData to fetchUserProfile # Add error handling to all API endpoints /batch add try-catch error handling to every Express route handler # Migrate imports across hundreds of files /batch update all imports from lodash to lodash-es Each agent works on a subset of files independently. Changes are coordinated and merged back. Best for mechanical, repetitive changes across many files. Plugins ▼ Extend Claude Code with community and first-party plugins that add skills, commands, tools, and integrations. # Browse and install plugins /plugin # Reload plugins without restarting Claude /reload-plugins # Remove orphaned auto-installed plugin dependencies claude plugin prune claude plugin uninstall my-plugin --prune # uninstall + cascade # Load plugins from a directory or .zip archive claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugins claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin.zip # .zip archives also accepted # Fetch and load a plugin from a URL (current session only) claude --plugin-url https://example.com/my-plugin.zip # Disable a plugin (blocked if another enabled plugin depends on it — shows chain hint) claude plugin disable my-plugin # Enable a plugin (auto-enables all transitive dependencies) claude plugin enable my-plugin # Scaffold a new plugin in .claude/skills/ claude plugin init my-plugin Auto-load from .claude/skills/ : plugin directories placed in .claude/skills/ are automatically loaded without marketplace registration or claude plugin install . Commit them to the repo so every teammate gets them automatically (v2.1.157). /reload-plugins LSP handling (v2.1.243): No longer keeps the LSP tool registered after the last LSP plugin is disabled. Reloading now also warns before an LSP plugin change that would cause the conversation to be re-read. Archive plugin source: install a plugin persistently from a zip over HTTPS — no git or npm required. Add an archive -type source to your plugin config pointing at the zip URL; optionally pin it with a SHA-256 hash for integrity verification (v2.1.224). Unlike --plugin-url (session-only, above), this registers the plugin as a normal persistent source. Command plugin source: add a command -type source that runs a local command (e.g. one supplied by an IDE) to print the plugin directory. The directory is re-resolved every session and applied without a restart, so it stays in sync with whatever the command reports. Set "mode": "link" to use the resolved directory in place rather than copying it (v2.1.229). Marketplace headersHelper : a url marketplace or catalog entry can declare a headersHelper command that mints HTTP headers (e.g. a short-lived token) for catalog and same-origin archive fetches. A catalog entry's helper runs only when you install or update that plugin, after its command is shown; claude plugin install / update prompt [y/N] (or pass -y ). MCP headersHelper in a project .mcp.json now requires that folder's trust dialog to have been accepted (also under claude -p ), and runs without inherited credential env vars; user, managed, and claude.ai-scope helpers now run from the Claude config dir (v2.1.238). Cloud-synced plugins: plugins synced from claude.ai into cloud sessions now display as name@synced in plugin listings and can be targeted directly with claude plugin enable/disable <name>@synced ; a synced plugin never overrides a same-named plugin you installed locally (v2.1.239). Plugins add skills invokable via /skill-name Executables under bin/ are invokable as bare commands Plugin marketplace for discovery and one-click install Root-level skill shortcut: a plugin with a top-level SKILL.md and no skills/ subdirectory is automatically surfaced as a skill — no directory structure required for single-skill plugins claude plugin details <name> shows the plugin's component inventory: skills, MCP servers, LSP servers, and projected per-session token cost. The marketplace browse and discover panes now show a full component preview (commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP/LSP servers) before installation, along with per-turn and per-invocation token estimates and when each plugin was last updated — useful for comparing plugin overhead and freshness before committing. Reserved MCP server name: workspace is reserved — an mcpServers entry named workspace will be skipped with a warning at startup; rename it to avoid silent breakage Default folder override warning: if plugin.json explicitly sets a key (e.g. "commands" ) that matches a default component folder, that default folder is silently skipped. Claude Code v2.1.140 now warns when this happens — visible in /doctor , claude plugin list , and /plugin . If the override is intentional, no action is needed. Dependency enforcement: claude plugin disable is blocked when another enabled plugin depends on the target — the error includes a copy-pasteable chain command showing what to disable first. claude plugin enable automatically force-enables all transitive dependencies. Fixed in v2.1.243: dependencies declared via a plugin's marketplace field now resolve correctly when both the dependent and depended-on plugin are loaded together via --plugin-dir (previously these never resolved). Scaffold a plugin locally: claude plugin init <name> creates a new plugin skeleton in .claude/skills/<name>/ — no marketplace required. Generates plugin.json , a starter SKILL.md , and the standard directory layout ready for customization (v2.1.157). Marketplace search bar: the /plugin marketplace view includes a search bar for filtering plugins by name — no more scrolling through long lists (v2.1.172). MCP server alwaysLoad option — set "alwaysLoad": true in an MCP server config to make all its tools skip tool-search deferral and stay permanently available. Useful for servers whose tools you use in nearly every session. { "mcpServers": { "my-server": { "command": "npx", "args": ["my-mcp-server"], "alwaysLoad": true } } } Voice Input ▼ Dictate prompts instead of typing. Push-to-talk voice input with support for 20+ languages. # Enable voice mode /voice # Then hold Space to talk, release to send # Rebind the key in ~/.claude/keybindings.json: # { "voice:pushToTalk": "ctrl+space" } Supports English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Russian, Polish, Turkish, Dutch, Ukrainian, Greek, Czech, Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, and more. Context Management ▼ Monitor and optimize your context window to keep sessions productive as they grow. # Visualize context usage with optimization tips /context # Compress context — keep only what matters /compact /compact "focus on the auth module" # Auto-compact via hooks when context gets large # PreCompact and PostCompact hooks fire around compaction /context shows token counts, heavy tools, and memory bloat analysis /compact with a focus string preserves relevant context while trimming the rest Status line can display live context usage with a color-coded progress bar Auto-compact is toggleable in /config — when it is off, the context-limit error says so and points you there (v2.1.235) Sonnet 5's default auto-compact window now uses its full 1M-token context — sessions on the 1M window auto-compact at about 967K tokens instead of about 934K (v2.1.247) Monitor Tool — Background Script Streaming ▼ The Monitor tool streams stdout events from a script started with Bash(run_in_background: true) . Each line of output arrives as a notification, letting Claude observe long-running processes without blocking the conversation. # Ask Claude to run tests in the background and watch them "Run the test suite in the background and tell me when done" # Claude uses Bash(run_in_background: true) to launch tests, # then Monitor streams each stdout line back as it arrives Observe CI pipelines, build scripts, and dev servers without blocking React to output in real time — fail fast on errors, summarize on completion Pairs with Ctrl+B for manually backgrounded tasks Subprocess Sandboxing ▼ Claude Code supports OS-level sandboxing that restricts what Bash subprocesses can read, write, and reach on the network — enforced by Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux / WSL2. Run /sandbox to enable it and choose a mode. Linux and WSL2 users must first install the required packages: sudo apt-get install bubblewrap socat (Ubuntu/Debian) or sudo dnf install bubblewrap socat (Fedora). Bash tool permission checking was also improved for zsh-specific syntax in shell conditionals, reducing false permission prompts for zsh-style conditional commands (v2.1.238). As of v2.1.246, Bash permission checks always require approval for malformed commands with a dangling && or || operator, closing a gap where a syntactically-broken compound command could otherwise skip the intended approval flow. Sandbox modes Mode Behavior Auto-allow Sandboxed bash commands run automatically without approval prompts. Commands that cannot be sandboxed (e.g. need access to non-allowed network hosts) fall back to the normal permission flow. rm targeting critical paths still prompts. Regular permissions All bash commands go through the standard permission flow even when sandboxed — more control, more prompts. The sandbox still enforces the same filesystem and network boundaries. Key settings.json keys Setting key Effect sandbox.enabled Enable sandboxing ( true / false ). Equivalent to using /sandbox interactively. sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite Array of paths (absolute, ~/ , or ./ relative to project) that subprocess commands may write to outside the working directory — e.g. ["~/.kube", "/tmp/build"] . Arrays merge across config scopes. sandbox.filesystem.denyRead Block subprocess read access to specified paths — e.g. ["~/"] to prevent reading outside the project. As of v2.1.236 (macOS), wildcard denyRead rules (e.g. **/.env ) take precedence even inside an allowRead region, cover the contents of matched directories, and can't be bypassed by renaming the denied file. sandbox.filesystem.allowRead Re-allow reads within a denyRead region — e.g. ["."] to permit the current project while blocking the rest of ~/ . sandbox.filesystem.disabled Set to true to skip filesystem isolation entirely while keeping network egress control active — useful when allowedDomains is your primary security boundary but filesystem sandboxing causes compatibility issues (v2.1.216). sandbox.network.allowedDomains Allowlist of domains Bash subprocesses may reach. New domain requests trigger a permission prompt; use allowManagedDomainsOnly: true to block unapproved domains automatically. As of v2.1.191, hosts approved interactively with "Yes" during a session are remembered for the rest of that session — no re-prompting on subsequent connections to the same host. As of v2.1.243, the sandboxed Bash tool prompt no longer pre-lists the full set of allowed hosts — Claude simply attempts a request and you approve new hosts as they come up, rather than assuming an unlisted host is blocked. sandbox.network.deniedDomains Block specific domains even when an allowedDomains wildcard would otherwise permit them — useful for blocking telemetry or third-party endpoints in CI. sandbox.network.strictAllowlist Set to true to silently deny all network connections from sandboxed commands to non-allowlisted hosts — no permission prompt is shown. Stricter than the default behavior; use in high-security environments or CI where unexpected network access should fail hard rather than pause for user input (v2.1.219). sandbox.failIfUnavailable Set to true to make sandbox startup failure a hard error instead of a warning — intended for managed deployments that require sandboxing as a security gate. sandbox.bwrapPath (Linux/WSL only) Custom path to the bwrap (bubblewrap) binary — use when bubblewrap is installed in a non-standard location on managed systems or container base images. sandbox.socatPath (Linux/WSL only) Custom path to the socat binary — use when socat is installed in a non-standard location on managed systems or container base images. sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands Set to false to disable the escape hatch — Claude can no longer retry failed commands outside the sandbox. All commands must be sandboxed or listed in excludedCommands . sandbox.allowAppleEvents (macOS only) Set to true to allow sandboxed commands to send Apple Events — enables open , osascript , and browser-based auth flows that rely on Apple Events (v2.1.181) sandbox.credentials Set to false to block sandboxed commands from reading credential files (e.g. ~/.aws/credentials , ~/.ssh/id_rsa ) and secret environment variables. Recommended in high-security or shared CI environments where subprocess access to credentials must be prevented (v2.1.187). Beyond block/allow, credential files can be masked instead: mode: "mask" (Linux/WSL; macOS falls back to deny ) has sandboxed commands read a sentinel copy while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress (v2.1.221). As of v2.1.224, masking supports extract / onExtractNoMatch for structured env values, decode: "jwt" with maskClaims for JWT-aware masking, and awsPairs / sigv4 for AWS SigV4 re-signing — these require network.tlsTerminate . Hardening env vars (shared environments & CI/CD) Env Var Effect --restricted / CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1 Full lockdown mode: removes the built-in tools that run commands or code and WebFetch (unless explicitly named in --tools ), keeps file tools confined to the working directory, refuses bypassPermissions , and ignores user, project, and local settings files. Use for untrusted or high-risk automated contexts where no code execution or arbitrary network egress should be possible (v2.1.248). CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 Enables PID namespace isolation on Linux — sandboxed commands can't see or signal processes outside their namespace CLAUDE_CODE_SCRIPT_CAPS=N Limits total script invocations per session to N — prevents runaway automation CLAUDE_CODE_HIDE_CWD=1 Hides the working directory path from the startup logo — useful in CI/CD and shared environments where paths should not be exposed DISABLE_UPDATES=1 Completely blocks all update paths including manual claude update . Stricter than DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER (which only prevents auto-updates). Use in managed/enterprise environments to pin a specific version. CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE=1 On Homebrew or WinGet installations, runs the package manager upgrade in the background and prompts to restart when a new version is ready. Complement to DISABLE_UPDATES — use when you want managed automatic updates. ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER Select Bedrock service tier: default | flex | priority . Sent as the X-Amzn-Bedrock-Service-Tier header. Use priority for provisioned-capacity deployments. ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX Have Bedrock prefer a specific cross-region inference profile over the one derived automatically from AWS_REGION . Set to the desired region prefix (e.g. us , eu ) (v2.1.224). CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT=1 Force-enables synchronized output mode for terminals where auto-detection fails (e.g. Emacs eat ). Fixes garbled or interleaved output in unsupported terminal emulators. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1 Opts out of the fullscreen alternate-screen renderer — keeps the conversation in the terminal's native scrollback buffer instead. Useful in tmux, GNU screen, or CI environments where alternate-screen mode interferes with log capture. CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS Clone GitHub plugin sources over HTTPS instead of SSH — use in environments where a GitHub SSH key is unavailable (CI/CD containers, managed desktops, devcontainers). ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID Workload identity federation — scopes the minted auth token to a specific workspace when a federation rule covers more than one. Set in managed enterprise deployments using identity federation for authentication. CLAUDE_CODE_POWERSHELL_RESPECT_EXECUTION_POLICY=1 Opts out of the default -ExecutionPolicy Bypass flag Claude Code passes to PowerShell. Use in environments with enforced PowerShell execution policy (e.g. AllSigned or RemoteSigned) where bypass is not permitted. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=0 Disables the PowerShell tool entirely. The tool is now enabled by default on Windows for Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry users — use this opt-out in environments where PowerShell access is prohibited. CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP=N Maximum number of consecutive stop-hook blocks before the turn ends with a warning. Default: 8 . Raise the cap if your stop hook legitimately needs more retry cycles; set to 1 to fail fast. CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 Deprecated as of v2.1.207. Auto mode is now available by default on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Foundry — no opt-in flag needed. To disable auto mode on these platforms, use disableAutoMode: true in ~/.claude/settings.json instead. (Previously required to enable auto mode on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry for Opus 4.7/4.8 — v2.1.158.) API_FORCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 Opts out of the default 5-minute idle timeout on Vertex AI and Foundry deployments (restored in v2.1.169). Stalled streams abort automatically after 5 minutes by default — set to 0 to disable the timeout for long-running batch jobs or custom streaming pipelines. CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE Desktop presence — path to a marker file that signals you're at the machine. When the file exists, Claude Code suppresses mobile push notifications. Create the file at session start and delete it when you step away (v2.1.181) CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG For unattended / CI sessions that need more than 15 retry attempts. Set to an integer (e.g. 30 ) to allow that many retries. Use this instead of CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES , which is now capped at 15 and should not be set higher. Designed for long-running automation where transient API errors should not abort a session (v2.1.186). As of v2.1.239, retries stop immediately on organization spend-limit and out-of-credits errors instead of waiting indefinitely for a reset — these are treated as unrecoverable rather than transient. CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT Override the default 5-minute abort timeout for remote MCP tool calls that produce no response. Set to an integer number of milliseconds (e.g. 300000 for 5 min). Increase for slow or high-latency MCP servers; decrease in CI to fail fast on unresponsive tools (v2.1.187). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1 Disables automatic memory-pressure reaping of idle background shell commands. By default, Claude Code terminates idle background shells when the system is under memory pressure. Set this to preserve long-running background shells (e.g. persistent dev servers) at the cost of higher memory usage (v2.1.193). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS=1 Disables mouse click, drag, and hover events in fullscreen mode while preserving mouse-wheel scroll. Set this in terminals where accidental clicks disrupt the interface — you keep scroll-only mouse interaction in fullscreen TUI sessions (v2.1.195). CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER Path to an executable that wraps every Claude Code self-spawn — agent view workers and background-service sessions run through this wrapper instead of invoking the binary directly. Use for corporate launchers, security wrappers, audit proxies, or environment injectors that must intercept all spawned subprocesses (v2.1.208). CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION Per-session cap on WebSearch tool calls. Default 200 ; set to a lower integer to prevent runaway search loops in unattended or agentic sessions (v2.1.212). CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION Hard cap removed in v2.1.224 — long-running sessions no longer refuse new agents once this budget is spent. Originally a per-session cap on subagent spawns (default 200 , resetting on /clear ) introduced in v2.1.212; concurrency ( CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS ) and nesting-depth ( CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH ) limits still apply. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS Cap on concurrently-running subagents within a session. Default 20 ; set to a lower integer to prevent a single message from fanning out unbounded background agents (v2.1.217). CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH Maximum nesting depth for subagent spawning. Default 1 — subagents do not spawn nested subagents by default. Set to 2 or higher to re-enable hierarchical agent architectures like orchestrator → specialist → worker trees (v2.1.217). CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS Threshold (ms) at which a long-running MCP tool call is automatically moved to the background so the session stays usable. Default 120000 (2 minutes). Set to 0 to disable auto-backgrounding and keep MCP calls in the foreground indefinitely (v2.1.212). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT Holds every Claude model with a native 1M-token context window to 200K via auto-compaction, not just a fixed list of models (broadened in v2.1.223). Use when you want consistent 200K-equivalent compaction behavior regardless of which 1M-capable model is active. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 As of v2.1.223, auto-compact keeps sessions on unrecognized model IDs within the assumed context window by default (a startup warning appears if this isn't holding the session to the expected size). Set this var to restore the previous behavior, letting unrecognized-model sessions grow past the assumed window unmanaged. CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH Maximum byte length of content attributes in OpenTelemetry log events. Default 61440 (60 KB). Increase for richer trace data in low-volume pipelines; decrease to cap payload size in high-throughput environments (v2.1.214). CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT Opt-in memory cgroup support for Bash tool commands on Linux — caps subprocess memory usage so a runaway build or process can't stall the session (v2.1.233). CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS Configures the WebFetch tool's session-scoped URL content cache TTL, in milliseconds. Default unchanged at 900000 (15 minutes). Lower it to force more frequent re-fetches of URLs that change often; raise it for long sessions repeatedly referencing the same slow-changing pages. Distinct from the Prompt Caching & KV Cache collapsible's ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H / FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M — that mechanism caches prompt/model context on Anthropic's side, not WebFetch's local URL-content cache (v2.1.233). CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME Optional short name for this project's per-project transcript directory under ~/.claude/projects/ . Intended for hosts that give each session its own config directory — set it to keep transcript paths short and readable instead of a long slug derived from the full working-directory path (v2.1.234). CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES Minutes a /goal may sit blocked on background tasks before Claude checks in on them instead of waiting indefinitely. Default 30 ; set to 0 to opt out and restore indefinite waiting. Useful in unattended sessions where a stalled background task would otherwise silently park a goal forever (v2.1.234). Best practice Start with /sandbox in Auto-allow mode and a narrow allowedDomains list. Add allowWrite paths only for tools that genuinely need them (e.g. ~/.kube for kubectl). Use deniedDomains to close loopholes left by broad wildcards, and set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false in managed environments where no escape hatch is acceptable. Prompt Caching & KV Cache ▼ Claude maintains a key-value (KV) cache of computed attention states for the leading prefix of each conversation. When a new request shares the same prefix as a cached one, Claude skips recomputing that prefix — delivering faster responses at roughly 10% of the regular input-token cost for cached tokens. The cache is prefix-based: content must appear at the beginning of the prompt to be cacheable. The first matching request in a window incurs a small cache-write overhead; every subsequent request within the TTL window is a cheap cache read. What gets cached in a Claude Code session System prompt injected by Claude Code at session start CLAUDE.md files loaded from the project and user config Large read-only documents attached at the top of the conversation Accumulated conversation history prefix (up to the last assistant turn) TTL configuration Env Var Effect ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 Opt into 1-hour prompt cache TTL (API key, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry). Improves hit rate for long or repeated sessions. FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 Force 5-minute TTL regardless of other settings. promptCacheTtl (settings.json) Set the main conversation's prompt cache TTL to 1 hour (API key and cloud-provider users). Equivalent to ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H but configured in settings.json (v2.1.243). subagentPromptCacheTtl (settings.json) Set subagent prompt cache TTL independently of the main conversation — subagents default to 5 minutes even when the main session uses a 1-hour TTL (v2.1.243). experimental.cacheTtl (agent frontmatter) Set a prompt cache TTL ( "5m" or "1h" ) for one specific agent, overriding the session-wide subagentPromptCacheTtl default when that setting isn't configured. Use when only a subset of your agents benefit from a longer TTL (v2.1.248). Choosing your TTL TTL Best for 5 min (default) Short one-off sessions; acceptable when sessions rarely outlast 5 minutes; lowest storage overhead. 1 hour Long coding sessions, nightly CI pipelines, any workflow where Claude re-reads the same large codebase context repeatedly. Enable whenever a session is likely to outlast 5 minutes or runs on a schedule. Persisting your TTL setting Set the env var once in a .env file at the project root — Claude Code reads this file automatically at startup: # .env (project root — add to .gitignore) ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 For a global default across all projects, export from your shell profile ( ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc ): export ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 Structuring Prompts for Maximum Cache Hits Stable content first — system prompt, CLAUDE.md, and large reference docs must form a leading prefix; dynamic content (task description, user message) goes last. Multi-user / CI deployments — use --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections to strip per-user dynamic injections so the shared system-prompt prefix is cacheable across all users. Observe cache activity — OTEL events include cacheRead and cacheCreation token breakdowns under claude_code.token.usage so you can confirm cache hits in your monitoring.

title: Agent Teams
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: Agent Teams ▼ Multiple Claude instances collaborating on the same codebase. Each agent works independently with its own context, but they share the same repo and can coordinate through files. Frontend + backend agents working in parallel Writer + reviewer pattern: one implements, another reviews Research agent gathers context while implementation agent builds Nested sub-agents: sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents, enabling hierarchical architectures like orchestrator → specialist → worker trees. Nesting is disabled by default as of v2.1.217 — set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=2 (or higher) to allow it; max depth was 5 levels in earlier versions (v2.1.172, updated v2.1.217) Subagent forking: as of v2.1.232, forking is on by default — a subagent_type: "fork" subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache from its parent instead of starting fresh, and non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now also run in the background by default. Cross-session SendMessage : as of v2.1.224, Claude Code sessions can message each other across any of your machines — not just teammates in the same tmux/worktree setup. Use ListAgents to discover reachable sessions. As of v2.1.225, you can start a conversation with a Remote Control session on another machine by name, instead of only replying after it messages you first — ListAgents shows Remote Control sessions as name [ref] . As of v2.1.228, cross-session messages display the sender and body inline, and messages to Remote Control sessions show your Remote Control session name as the sender. As of v2.1.232, typing @ in the prompt to mention any live session by name (not just teammates) resolves through SendMessage automatically, delivery to a bare name matching exactly one live session no longer waits for ref confirmation, and a session started or renamed to a name already in use on that machine gets a unique name-word-word variant automatically. As of v2.1.234, ListAgents and SendMessage report when your account's session list was too long to enumerate completely, so an unseen session is no longer silently treated as absent — a failed lookup is now distinguishable from a genuinely missing session. As of v2.1.235, SendMessage refuses a message too large for cross-session delivery up front, rather than accepting it and silently dropping it. As of v2.1.236, SendMessage accepts a notify_when_idle option: ask another Claude Code session on this machine to send one notice when it next goes idle — opt-in, one-shot, no polling (macOS and Linux). Available on macOS and Linux. As of v2.1.238, ListAgents and SendMessage now correctly list and reach Remote Control peers from server-mode ( claude remote-control ) and Desktop/IDE-hosted sessions instead of reporting "Remote Control is not connected", no longer expose the idle worker pre-warmed for your next background session until a task claims it, and report a refusal or dropped-inbox failure back to the sender instead of a silent success or a message vanishing. As of v2.1.239, cross-session messaging is available on Windows, reaching parity with macOS and Linux — Windows sessions can message each other with SendMessage and discover each other with ListAgents . ListAgents and /list-agents now correctly include your live teammates in the listing (previously only subagents and other sessions appeared, making a reachable teammate look absent). ListAgents also now tells a session its own addressable name, and SendMessage to your own name reports that instead of "no agent named …". As of v2.1.247, cross-session peer messages collapse by default to a one-line Message from @<sender>: <first line> preview; press Ctrl+O to expand the full body. As of v2.1.248, cross-session messaging ( SendMessage / ListAgents ) between sessions on the same machine is available on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry is disabled — previously limited to direct Anthropic API sessions. Also as of v2.1.248, when a subagent calls SendMessage to another session, any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to the subagent — worth knowing when a subagent-initiated cross-session conversation needs a response the subagent itself won't see. # Spawn a teammate in its own worktree + tmux pane claude -w feature-auth --tmux # Or run teammates in-process (no tmux needed) claude --teammate-mode in-process # Reference named agents with @ in your prompt # Team leader's model and permissions cascade to teammates # Message another running session by name/id SendMessage (to: "<agent-name-or-id>" , ...) # Discover reachable sessions across machines ListAgents () 🔗 Agent Teams Documentation Official docs on configuring and using agent teams

title: Work Trees
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: Work Trees ▼ Isolated git worktrees for parallel work. Each agent gets its own branch and working directory. Changes merge back when complete. # Start Claude in a new worktree claude -w feature-name # Pair with tmux for side-by-side terminals claude -w feature-name --tmux # Each worktree is a full repo checkout # Agents can work simultaneously without conflicts # Changes are merged back via standard git merge/PR worktree.baseRef setting — controls the branch base for all worktrees ( --worktree , EnterWorktree , and agent-isolation worktrees). Set in .claude/settings.json : Value Branches from When to use fresh (default) origin/<default-branch> Clean base — agents always start from the canonical remote state, no local noise head Local HEAD Share unpushed scaffolding — spawned agents inherit commits you haven't pushed yet worktree.bgIsolation setting — controls whether background sessions run in an isolated worktree or edit the working copy directly. Set in .claude/settings.json : Value Behavior When to use worktree (default) Background sessions run in an isolated git worktree via EnterWorktree Most repos — prevents conflicts with your working copy none Background sessions edit the working copy directly, no worktree created Monorepos with non-relocatable build artifacts or tools that cannot run from a worktree path Tip Worktrees are automatically cleaned up when the agent completes with no changes. If changes were made, the worktree path and branch are returned. WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks fire on lifecycle events. As of v2.1.157, EnterWorktree can switch between Claude-managed worktrees mid-session — an agent can hop from one task-worktree to another without stopping and restarting. As of v2.1.161, parallel tool calls are independent — a failed Bash command no longer cancels other calls in the same batch; each tool returns its own result. As of v2.1.211, "always allow" permission grants are saved at the repository root — approvals made inside a worktree persist across all sessions and worktrees for that repo. As of v2.1.221, background sessions commit and push to preserve their work, open a draft PR only when the task calls for one, follow your CLAUDE.md git instructions, and always end by reporting where the work lives. As of v2.1.238, worktree-isolation Bash refusals no longer tell you to remove a redirect when the command had none.

title: /loop — Built-in Scheduler (alias: /proactive)
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: /loop — Built-in Scheduler (alias: /proactive) ▼ Run commands on a recurring basis. Session-scoped — terminal must stay active. # Check for new issues every hour /loop 1h check for new Git issues and triage them # Run tests every 30 minutes and fix failures /loop 30m check if the codebase passes all tests, if not, fix it # Monitor deployment status /loop 15m check the deploy pipeline status and notify me of failures Cancel a Wakeup Press Esc while a /loop is counting down to cancel the pending wakeup without ending the session. For Persistence Session-scoped loops stop when the terminal closes. For persistent cloud scheduling, use /schedule to create cron-based tasks that run without an active terminal. Monitor Loop Cost /usage has a dedicated Loops breakdown (per-loop run count, total tokens, tokens per run, last run) as of v2.1.243 — check it if a /loop task seems to be running more often or costing more than expected. Available Everywhere Self-paced dynamic mode (no fixed interval — Claude paces itself) and the no-prompt autonomous default are now always available for /loop , including on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (v2.1.248).

title: Dynamic Workflows — Parallel Multi-Agent Orchestration
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: Dynamic Workflows — Parallel Multi-Agent Orchestration ▼ Dynamic workflows run tens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session — tackling problems too large for a single-pass solution. Claude decomposes the prompt, distributes subtasks across agents working simultaneously, verifies results through independent checking and adversarial refutation, and iterates until answers converge. "Work you'd normally plan in quarters now finishes in days." # Ask Claude directly to create a workflow "Create a workflow to find all security vulnerabilities across the codebase" "Create a workflow to migrate all API calls from v1 to v2" # Or enable ultracode — Claude decides when to use workflows automatically /effort ultracode Best-fit use cases Category Examples Codebase analysis Bug hunts, security audits, optimization reviews across entire services Large migrations Framework swaps, API deprecations, language ports spanning thousands of files Critical validation Independent multi-angle attempts when wrong answers carry high costs Token Cost Dynamic workflows can consume substantially more tokens than a typical Claude Code session. Available on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans . On Enterprise, off by default at launch — admins enable via Claude Code settings. Trigger keyword: ultracode Type the word ultracode in the prompt input (it highlights violet) to let Claude decide when to run a full dynamic workflow automatically. Press Alt+W or Backspace immediately after the keyword appears to dismiss an accidental trigger. To disable the keyword entirely, go to /config → Workflow keyword trigger . (v2.1.160) The built-in workflow prompt keyword uses a purple shimmer highlight and only fires on explicit phrases like "run a workflow" or "workflow:" — casual mentions of "workflow" in conversation no longer trigger it, reducing accidental activations (v2.1.178). Fan-outs now stagger same-prefix sibling agents so later agents read the cached prompt prefix instead of re-paying it, cutting redundant token cost across large parallel dispatches. Set CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS=0 to disable the staggering (v2.1.229).

title: Plugins
label: 14 — Claude Power Usage
text: Plugins ▼ Extend Claude Code with community and first-party plugins that add skills, commands, tools, and integrations. # Browse and install plugins /plugin # Reload plugins without restarting Claude /reload-plugins # Remove orphaned auto-installed plugin dependencies claude plugin prune claude plugin uninstall my-plugin --prune # uninstall + cascade # Load plugins from a directory or .zip archive claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugins claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin.zip # .zip archives also accepted # Fetch and load a plugin from a URL (current session only) claude --plugin-url https://example.com/my-plugin.zip # Disable a plugin (blocked if another enabled plugin depends on it — shows chain hint) claude plugin disable my-plugin # Enable a plugin (auto-enables all transitive dependencies) claude plugin enable my-plugin # Scaffold a new plugin in .claude/skills/ claude plugin init my-plugin Auto-load from .claude/skills/ : plugin directories placed in .claude/skills/ are automatically loaded without marketplace registration or claude plugin install . Commit them to the repo so every teammate gets them automatically (v2.1.157). /reload-plugins LSP handling (v2.1.243): No longer keeps the LSP tool registered after the last LSP plugin is disabled. Reloading now also warns before an LSP plugin change that would cause the conversation to be re-read. Archive plugin source: install a plugin persistently from a zip over HTTPS — no git or npm required. Add an archive -type source to your plugin config pointing at the zip URL; optionally pin it with a SHA-256 hash for integrity verification (v2.1.224). Unlike --plugin-url (session-only, above), this registers the plugin as a normal persistent source. Command plugin source: add a command -type source that runs a local command (e.g. one supplied by an IDE) to print the plugin directory. The directory is re-resolved every session and applied without a restart, so it stays in sync with whatever the command reports. Set "mode": "link" to use the resolved directory in place rather than copying it (v2.1.229). Marketplace headersHelper : a url marketplace or catalog entry can declare a headersHelper command that mints HTTP headers (e.g. a short-lived token) for catalog and same-origin archive fetches. A catalog entry's helper runs only when you install or update that plugin, after its command is shown; claude plugin install / update prompt [y/N] (or pass -y ). MCP headersHelper in a project .mcp.json now requires that folder's trust dialog to have been accepted (also under claude -p ), and runs without inherited credential env vars; user, managed, and claude.ai-scope helpers now run from the Claude config dir (v2.1.238). Cloud-synced plugins: plugins synced from claude.ai into cloud sessions now display as name@synced in plugin listings and can be targeted directly with claude plugin enable/disable <name>@synced ; a synced plugin never overrides a same-named plugin you installed locally (v2.1.239). Plugins add skills invokable via /skill-name Executables under bin/ are invokable as bare commands Plugin marketplace for discovery and one-click install Root-level skill shortcut: a plugin with a top-level SKILL.md and no skills/ subdirectory is automatically surfaced as a skill — no directory structure required for single-skill plugins claude plugin details <name> shows the plugin's component inventory: skills, MCP servers, LSP servers, and projected per-session token cost. The marketplace browse and discover panes now show a full component preview (commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP/LSP servers) before installation, along with per-turn and per-invocation token estimates and when each plugin was last updated — useful for comparing plugin overhead and freshness before committing. Reserved MCP server name: workspace is reserved — an mcpServers entry named workspace will be skipped with a warning at startup; rename it to avoid silent breakage Default folder override warning: if plugin.json explicitly sets a key (e.g. "commands" ) that matches a default component folder, that default folder is silently skipped. Claude Code v2.1.140 now warns when this happens — visible in /doctor , claude plugin list , and /plugin . If the override is intentional, no action is needed. Dependency enforcement: claude plugin disable is blocked when another enabled plugin depends on the target — the error includes a copy-pasteable chain command showing what to disable first. claude plugin enable automatically force-enables all transitive dependencies. Fixed in v2.1.243: dependencies declared via a plugin's marketplace field now resolve correctly when both the dependent and depended-on plugin are loaded together via --plugin-dir (previously these never resolved). Scaffold a plugin locally: claude plugin init <name> creates a new plugin skeleton in .claude/skills/<name>/ — no marketplace required. Generates plugin.json , a starter SKILL.md , and the standard directory layout ready for customization (v2.1.157). Marketplace search bar: the /plugin marketplace view includes a search bar for filtering plugins by name — no more scrolling through long lists (v2.1.172). MCP server alwaysLoad option — set "alwaysLoad": true in an MCP server config to make all its tools skip tool-search deferral and stay permanently available. Useful for servers whose tools you use in nearly every session. { "mcpServers": { "my-server": { "command": "npx", "args": ["my-mcp-server"], "alwaysLoad": true } } }
